name: Afghanistan
keyDate: No mandate
summary: Afghanistan has no e-invoicing mandate and no credible programme has been announced. The country operates a VAT system at a standard rate of 10 percent, with e-invoicing explicitly described as not mandatory. Monitoring continues for any future developments.

name: Åland Islands
keyDate: B2B from 1 July 2030 (EU ViDA)
authority: Finnish Tax Administration (Verohallinto) and State Treasury (Valtiokonttori) as Peppol Authority
summary: Åland Islands does not operate a separate e-invoicing regime and is administered under Finnish law for tax and invoicing purposes. Finland has a live B2G e-invoicing mandate under Act 241/2019, requiring all suppliers to public authorities to issue EN 16931-compliant structured e-invoices; this obligation has applied to all public bodies since April 2020 and was extended to full EN 16931 compliance for all B2G and qualifying B2B transactions from April 2021. There is no general B2B or B2C mandate, though any Finnish business with annual turnover above EUR 10,000 has a statutory right to demand structured e-invoices from its suppliers. No national ViDA implementing legislation has been published as of the source dates; EU-wide requirements are expected to apply from 1 July 2030.

name: Albania
keyDate: B2B since Mandatory since 2021
authority: General Directorate of Taxes (Drejtoria e Përgjithshme e Tatimeve)
summary: Albania operates a universal real-time fiscalisation system covering B2B, B2G and B2C transactions under Law No. 87/2019, administered through the General Directorate of Taxes' Central Information System (CIS). Invoices are submitted as UBL 2.1 XML, verified in real time, and assigned a unique NIVF identifier plus QR code before they are legally valid. Buyers of services from nonresident suppliers complete a reverse-charge invoice workflow inside the same platform, while imported goods have been subject to a fiscalisation procedure completable within seven days of entry into free circulation since January 2026. A separate 2025 measure requires transport and accommodation businesses to install POS terminals, with the obligation expected to extend to all businesses by end of 2026.

name: Algeria
keyDate: B2G issue since Since January 2023 (voluntary)
summary: Successive finance laws signal a move toward electronic invoicing; the implementing framework is still awaited. Optional B2G e-invoicing for public contracts has been reported since 2023. The original January 2026 mandatory target was missed and no binding legislation has been published; secondary sources now treat compulsory rollout as unlikely before 2027.

name: American Samoa
keyDate: No mandate
authority: American Samoa Government Tax Office, Department of the Treasury
summary: American Samoa operates its own independent tax administration, modelled on the US Internal Revenue Code as it stood on 31 December 2000, but with distinct territorial provisions administered by the American Samoa Government Tax Office. No e-invoicing mandate, platform, voluntary framework, or credible programme of any kind has been identified in any available official source. The territory remains entirely outside the scope of e-invoicing regulation as of August 2026.

name: Andorra
keyDate: B2G issue from 1 January 2027
summary: Andorra has no domestic B2B e-invoicing or transaction level CTC mandate, and the tax authority has not announced a parallel EU style roadmap as of 2026. Public sector invoicing is already live for the general administration through the official invoice portal and register that opened on 1 October 2024, with the obligation in force from 1 January 2025. Communes, dependent entities, and other public bodies were extended to 1 January 2027, and some entities still accept electronically signed PDF invoices until structured e-invoicing is fully in place.

name: Angola
keyDate: B2G since Presidential Decree No. 71/25 (20 March 2025) effective mid-September 2025; Phase 1 mandatory 1 January 2026 for large taxpayers (turnover ≥ Kz 350 million), government suppliers, and very-high-value invoices (≥ Kz 25 million); Phase 2 extends to all remaining VAT-registered businesses by 1 January 2027
model: Post-clearance — invoices generated via AGT-certified software, transmitted to AGT for registration then content validation; rejected/invalid invoices are treated as not issued
format: JSON (for AGT data exchange); human-readable versions (e.g. PDF) must include a specified QR code
authority: Administração Geral Tributária (AGT) — General Tax Administration
summary: Angola is implementing a phased mandatory e-invoicing system under Presidential Decree No. 71/25 (20 March 2025), with detailed technical rules set out in Executive Decree 683/25. The Decree became effective mid-September 2025 (six months after publication), followed by a "soft landing" transition period (1 October-31 December 2025) during which businesses could use old invoice formats without penalty while the General Tax Administration (AGT) finalised software certification. Phase 1 became mandatory from 1 January 2026, applying to large taxpayers (annual turnover ≥ Kz 350 million), government suppliers (B2G), and any invoice of very high value (≥ Kz 25 million) regardless of issuer size. Phase 2 runs September 2026-January 2027, extending the mandate to all remaining VAT-registered businesses under the General or Simplified VAT regimes by 1 January 2027. The system operates a post-clearance model: invoices are generated via AGT-certified software in JSON format, transmitted to AGT for registration and then content validation, with rejected or invalid invoices treated as not issued at all.

name: Anguilla
keyDate: No mandate
summary: Anguilla has no e-invoicing mandate, platform, or programme of any kind. The territory operates its own Inland Revenue Department, levies no income tax and no VAT, and relies instead on a Goods and Services Tax together with various other indirect levies. No legal instrument introducing e-invoicing has been identified in any official source.

name: Antigua & Barbuda
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Antigua & Barbuda in the sources reviewed. The market-research report forecasts commercial e-invoicing software adoption, not a government mandate — no evidence of an actual legal requirement was found.

name: Argentina
keyDate: B2B issue from By July 2027
format: AFIP web services / ARCA XML (Comprobante Electrónico)
summary: Electronic invoicing with CAE authorisation codes is mandatory for virtually all taxpayers. Documents are authorised through AFIP web services (now ARCA) and issued as XML electronic receipts (Comprobante Electrónico). From 1 July 2026 General Resolution 5824/26 extends the mandate to further sectors and adds a monthly electronic settlement system, with more entities due by July 2027.

name: Armenia
keyDate: B2G since Mandatory since 2016
summary: Armenia operates a fully live, mandatory electronic invoicing system administered by the State Revenue Committee. E-invoicing has been compulsory for all businesses covering B2G, B2B, and B2C transactions since 2016, following an initial rollout for large taxpayers from 2010. The government-operated platform handles invoice creation, signing, transmission, and compliance validation in real time.

name: Aruba
keyDate: No mandate
summary: Aruba has no e-invoicing mandate, announced programme, or formal proposal as of August 2026. The Departamento di Impuesto (DIMP) launched the second phase of its online tax portal (BOi) in May 2026, representing a significant step toward digital tax administration, but this covers tax assessments, payment plans, and fiscal account management rather than e-invoicing. Aruba operates its own independent tax system based on a cumulative turnover tax (BBO/BAZV/BAVP) rather than a VAT, and no credible e-invoicing initiative has been identified in authoritative sources.

name: Australia
keyDate: B2G receive since large agencies from 1 July 2021
summary: Peppol e-invoicing is mandated across federal agencies for receipt from 1 July 2022 (large agencies from 1 July 2021) and promoted for B2B. Business mandates, including a Business eInvoicing Right (BER), were consulted in 2020 to 2022 but not legislated. The ATO is the Australian Peppol Authority; the format is Peppol PINT A-NZ.

name: Austria
keyDate: B2G issue since 18 April 2020
model: Portal submission via USP / e-Rechnung.gv.at or Peppol eDelivery network
summary: Austria mandated e-invoicing for federal government suppliers from 1 January 2014 under the IKT-Konsolidierungsgesetz, extended to all sub-central public authorities by 18 April 2020 in line with EU Directive 2014/55/EU. Invoices must be submitted via the USP portal or e-Rechnung.gv.at in ebInterface or Peppol BIS 3.0 format. B2B and B2C e-invoicing remain entirely voluntary, with no domestic mandate date announced; the EU ViDA package introduces cross-border digital reporting from 1 July 2030.

name: Azerbaijan
keyDate: B2B since In force since 1 April 2017
authority: State Tax Service (STS) under the Ministry of Economy
summary: Azerbaijan operates a fully live mandatory e-invoicing regime for all VAT-registered businesses across B2B and B2G transactions (B2C is out of scope for e-invoices, handled instead by real-time cash registers). Electronic tax invoices, known locally as e-qaimə or e-VHF, must be issued and submitted through the State Tax Service portal at e-taxes.gov.az, authenticated with an enhanced electronic signature (Asan İmza / SIMA Token), and are governed by Tax Code Article 218.1.2 (issuers) and Article 58 (financial sanctions). A VAT deposit-account split-payment mechanism (Cabinet of Ministers Decision No. 219/2007) requires the VAT portion of B2B payments to reach a Treasury-held account within one business day as a condition of input-VAT credit, backed by a 50% penalty for non-compliance. Non-resident B2C e-service providers face mandatory VAT registration from 23 August 2026 but do not issue Azerbaijani e-invoices themselves.

name: Bahamas
keyDate: No mandate
summary: The Bahamas has no e-invoicing or transaction-level continuous transaction control mandate in place, and no such programme has been announced or proposed. The Department of Inland Revenue administers VAT and other taxes through an online portal, but invoicing remains outside any structured digital mandate.

name: Bahrain
keyDate: Phased rollout anticipated from 2026; no confirmed date published by the NBR
summary: Bahrain's National Bureau for Revenue has confirmed that a B2B e-invoicing mandate is in development, with a phased rollout anticipated to begin in 2026, large taxpayers first. The NBR issued a tender in 2023 for the central e-invoicing platform, ran a business consultation/survey through 2024-2025, and the 2025/26 Budget signalled the mandate alongside other tax reforms including a possible VAT rate increase from the current 10%. One concrete change has already landed: the prior requirement for tax-authority approval before issuing e-invoices has been removed, opening a voluntary runway for businesses that want to exchange structured e-invoices before any mandate takes effect. As of August 2026, no detailed technical specifications, confirmed launch dates, or binding legal instrument have been formally published.

name: Bangladesh
keyDate: pilot 2023; phased from 2024; broader 2026 window pending NBR communications
summary: Bangladesh National Board of Revenue (NBR) is described as rolling out a national VAT electronic invoicing programme for B2B invoices, with a 2023 pilot and later waves of VAT registered businesses. The intended design is real time or near real time clearance linked to NBR VAT online filing. As of early 2026, binding go live dates, final XML or JSON specifications, and full scope mandate legislation were still evolving, so obligations should be confirmed with NBR.

name: Barbados
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Barbados in the sources reviewed. Official BRA and government portals confirm general online tax filing and payment infrastructure, but no source describes a structured e-invoicing mandate, format, or platform.

name: Belarus
keyDate: B2B issue since Since 2016
summary: Belarus operates a clearance-based e-invoicing system for VAT transactions through the national Electronic System of Invoices (ESCF). Invoices must be submitted to the Ministry of Taxes and Duties portal for approval before delivery to the recipient. The format is a national XML standard administered by NALOG.

name: Belgium
keyDate: B2B from 2030
summary: Structured B2B e-invoicing via the Peppol network became mandatory for all VAT-registered businesses established in Belgium on 1 January 2026, following legislation published in the Belgian Official Gazette on 20 February 2024. Invoices must comply with EN 16931, with Peppol BIS 3.0 as the default format, though other EN 16931-compliant formats are permitted by mutual agreement. A near-real-time e-reporting layer using a Peppol 5-corner model is planned for January 2028, and cross-border intra-EU B2B e-invoicing is expected to follow in January 2030 under the EU ViDA initiative.

name: Belize
keyDate: B2B issue from 2027 for large taxpayers; broader rollout timeline not yet published
summary: Belize has enacted the General Sales Tax (Amendment) Act, 2024 (Act No. 34 of 2024), in force from 1 January 2025, as the legal basis for mandatory e-invoicing under a centralised pre-clearance model. The Ministry of Finance reaffirmed the mandate for GST-registered businesses in the 10 March 2026 budget speech. Large taxpayers are targeted from 2027; technical specifications and the full phased schedule have not yet been published.

name: Benin
keyDate: B2B issue since 1 July 2021 (EDICOM; not stated on the DGI e-MECeF page)
format: e-MECeF (A4 PDF or approved SFE API)
summary: Benin requires taxpayers to issue standardized invoices (factures normalisées) through certified electronic invoicing machines (MECeF) or the DGI online platform e-MECeF. The DGI returns a MECeF/DGI code for invoices transmitted in the system. Businesses may invoice with the DGI e-SFE or with their own billing system once the DGI has approved it.

name: Bermuda
keyDate: No mandate
authority: Office of the Tax Commissioner (OTC), Bermuda
summary: Bermuda has no e-invoicing mandate, platform, or announced programme of any kind. The Office of the Tax Commissioner administers a range of taxes including payroll tax, land tax, and corporate services tax, and operates an online E-Tax payment and filing tool, but none of these involve e-invoicing obligations. Bermuda has no VAT and no goods-and-services tax, removing the principal regulatory driver that typically motivates e-invoicing mandates.

name: Bhutan
keyDate: Rollout underway as of early 2026; mandatory date not confirmed in sources
summary: Bhutan has no e-invoicing or transaction-level CTC mandate, and no credible programme has been announced. GST administration is digital for returns (RAMIS, BIRMS, BITS) and GovTech lists GST-compliant invoicing software; that is ordinary tax invoicing, not clearance or structured e-invoicing. We monitor for changes.

name: Bolivia
keyDate: B2B issue since exclusive online invoicing from 1 October 2026
summary: Bolivia operates a phased mandatory e-invoicing regime under the Virtual Invoicing System (SFV), administered by the National Tax Service (SIN). Large taxpayers have been live since December 2021, with eight further waves bringing additional groups online through October 2024. Taxpayer groups 9 through 12, comprising 27,973 taxpayers, had their compliance deadline extended to 1 October 2026 via Resolution No. 102600000007 published on 23 March 2026.

name: Bonaire, Sint Eustatius & Saba
keyDate: No mandate
summary: Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba (the BES islands) operate under a distinct tax regime administered by Belastingdienst Caribisch Nederland (BCN), a dedicated Caribbean Netherlands division of the Dutch Tax and Customs Administration. The principal indirect tax is the General Expenditure Tax (GET), not VAT, and EU law does not automatically apply to these territories. No e-invoicing mandate, pilot, platform, or credible programme has been identified in any available official or authoritative source.

name: Bosnia & Herzegovina
keyDate: B2B from Under preparation; FBiH apply by 31 Aug 2027
authority: ITA / FBiH Tax Administration / entity authorities
summary: E-invoicing and real-time reporting initiatives are under preparation at entity level; no binding countrywide mandate yet. The Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina enacted the Law on Fiscalization of Transactions (Official Gazette No. 9/26, published 4 February 2026, in force 12 February 2026) for B2B, B2G, and B2C via a Central Fiscalization Platform. Application starts only after implementing bylaws and infrastructure, no later than 31 August 2027; Republika Srpska and Brčko District keep separate fiscal systems.

name: Botswana
keyDate: B2B issue from EBS reported to commence 1 April 2027
summary: Botswana has moved electronic invoicing from budget plans into statute. The Tax Administration Act, 2026 (in force from 1 July 2026) defines an electronic invoice as one issued through a BURS approved Electronic Billing System. Related Regulations are reported to commence that system on 1 April 2027; BURS has not yet published the structured format, portal, or clearance rules.

name: Brazil
keyDate: B2B issue since 1 September 2026
summary: Brazil's NF-e (goods) and NFS-e (services) clearance model e-invoicing is mature and effectively universal, with SEFAZ validating invoices before legal issuance. NFCom is a separate mandatory e-invoice for telecom sector transactions. 2026 is the CBS/IBS dual VAT reform transition year at temporary token rates (CBS 0.9%, IBS 0.1%); Joint Act RFB/CGIBS No. 4/2026 sets five waves of mandatory IBS/CBS electronic tax document content from 3 August 2026 through 1 January 2027, while the broader reform phases through a multi year timetable with full consolidation expected by 2033. A narrow delay pushes some CBS registration and invoicing duties for individuals and rural producers to 1 January 2027, but this does not affect the broader reform timeline for companies, legal entities, foreign businesses or non resident digital service providers.

name: British Virgin Islands
keyDate: No mandate
summary: The British Virgin Islands has no e-invoicing mandate, platform, or announced programme. The territory's tax base consists of payroll tax, stamp duty, property tax, and similar levies but no VAT or general sales tax, leaving no structural foundation on which an e-invoicing obligation could be built. The Inland Revenue Department, operating under the BVI Ministry of Finance, administers these taxes but has published no e-invoicing initiative.

name: Brunei
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed; Brunei's Treasury Accounting and Financial Information System (TAFIS 2.0) includes an invoice-status-viewing feature for government financial processes, but this is not confirmed to be a structured e-invoicing or CTC system
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Brunei in the sources reviewed, despite the country's prior 'proposed'-adjacent classification research context (existing status recorded as 'none'). Brunei operates TAFIS (Treasury Accounting and Financial Information System, now on version 2.0, built on SAP), the government's core financial management system, which includes a feature to "VIEW INVOICE STATUS" — but the banked sources describe only system maintenance/downtime notices for TAFIS, with no substantive description of its invoicing functionality, no confirmation it constitutes structured e-invoicing, and no indication it extends to private-sector B2B transactions. Brunei is a member of ASEAN, a regional bloc where, per one industry source, e-invoicing implementation is generally described as being "in its initial phase" continent-wide, with only Singapore and Indonesia cited as having live mandates as of that source's review, and Brunei not mentioned among the five countries "planning to introduce it in the nearest time."

name: Bulgaria
keyDate: B2G receive since 1 November 2019
authority: NRA (National Revenue Agency); Ministry of Transport, Information Technology and Communications
summary: Bulgaria has no mandatory B2G, B2B, or B2C e-invoicing requirement for suppliers, though all public contracting authorities must receive and process EN 16931-compliant e-invoices since 1 November 2019. The National Revenue Agency is introducing phased SAF-T reporting obligations beginning with large taxpayers on 1 January 2026, with full rollout expected by 2030. A public consultation on a mandatory clearance-model B2B e-invoicing regime is underway, but no binding mandate or implementation date has yet been legislated.

name: Burkina Faso
keyDate: B2B issue since Phase 1
summary: Burkina Faso launched the Certified Electronic Invoice (FEC) system on 6 January 2026. From 1 July 2026, domestic taxpayers under the standard tax regime with annual turnover of at least XOF 50 million must issue certified invoices through SECeF, covering B2B, B2C and B2G flows according to the more complete secondary write ups. Later phases are not specified in the available sources.

name: Burundi
keyDate: B2B since EBMS mandatory since January 2022 for certain taxpayers; second phase launched 18 March 2025 (5,000 additional fiscal devices, total ~8,000, use now described as mandatory for traders)
model: Fiscal devices — real-time transmission of invoice data to OBR via the Electronic Billing Management System (EBMS)
summary: Burundi introduced the Electronic Billing Management System (EBMS) in January 2022, requiring certain taxpayers — including domestic and foreign providers of digitalised services — to submit invoice data in real time to the Office Burundais des Recettes (OBR). The system launched with over 200 taxpayers connected and has since expanded: a March 2025 second phase added 5,000 fiscal invoicing devices (on top of 3,000 already deployed), with OBR now describing device collection and use as mandatory for traders and warning of sanctions for non-compliance. Implementation has faced acknowledged challenges, and the system is still described as being in an adaptation phase.

name: Cambodia
keyDate: B2G issue since 2025 fiscal year onward (Circular No. 003); scope widened 14 July 2025
summary: Cambodia is phasing in CamInvoice, a national clearance platform: electronic invoices must be submitted, validated and approved before they are legally valid. Business to government use is already mandatory for designated central ministries and their suppliers under MEF circulars issued in 2025. Business to business use remains voluntary; a later private sector mandate is reported for 2026 for a defined group of taxpayers, but no circular in these sources fixes that date or the segment.

name: Cameroon
keyDate: 2026 (technical specifications and rollout pending)
model: CTC (central e-Facturation platform with accredited providers)
summary: Cameroon's 2026 Finance Law introduces mandatory real time electronic invoicing for all taxable persons. Every invoice, including taxable, VAT exempt, and out of scope supplies, must be issued through an approved system linked to a central e-Facturation platform, with accredited interoperable providers expected. Technical specifications, certification rules, and an operational start date have not been published.

name: Canada
keyDate: B2G issue since From end of 2018
format: Electronic submission via federal portal; UBL 2.1 available
summary: Canada has no mandatory e-invoicing regime for B2B transactions at the federal level. Federal suppliers must submit invoices to government electronically through a dedicated portal, but all other e-invoicing remains voluntary. The Canada Revenue Agency administers the Excise Tax Act and publishes guidance on electronic invoicing, while the Peppol network is available for voluntary adoption.

name: Cape Verde
keyDate: Decree Law 79/2020; reinforced 1 January 2026
summary: Cabo Verde requires electronic issuance and communication of fiscally relevant documents to the National Directorate of State Revenue (DNRE). The obligation originates in Decree Law 79/2020 and was reinforced by Law No. 69/X/2025 (the 2026 State Budget), which took effect on 1 January 2026. DNRE has confirmed that more than half a million electronic invoices have already been issued.

name: Cayman Islands
keyDate: No mandate
authority: Department for International Tax Cooperation (DITC), Cayman Islands
summary: The Cayman Islands has no e-invoicing mandate, platform, or announced programme. The territory levies no income tax, corporate tax, VAT, or GST, removing the fiscal basis on which e-invoicing obligations are typically constructed. The DITC focuses exclusively on international tax information exchange frameworks such as CRS, FATCA, Country-by-Country Reporting, and Economic Substance.

name: Central African Republic
keyDate: No mandate
authority: Direction Générale des Impôts et des Domaines (DGID)
summary: The Central African Republic has no e-invoicing or transaction-level continuous transaction control mandate in force, announced, or formally proposed. The tax authority, the Direction Générale des Impôts et des Domaines, completed a broader digital tax modernisation project in 2023 that introduced an eTax platform for online registration, electronic declarations, and payments, but this does not constitute a structured e-invoicing obligation. No legislative instrument, rollout date, or technical format requirement has been identified in the available sources.

name: Chad
keyDate: B2G issue since 1 January 2026
authority: Direction Générale des Impôts (DGI) / Ministry of Finance, Chad
summary: Chad's 2026 Finance Law, promulgated by President Mahamat Déby and effective 1 January 2026, expanded the mandatory use of the Standardized Electronic Invoice (Facture Électronique Normalisée, FEN) to cover public expenditure processing, public bodies, autonomous local authorities, NGOs, associations, and liberal professions. Suppliers to public contracts must register with the FEN system, and non-compliant invoices are rejected within the public expenditure chain. The technical model and detailed format specification beyond the FEN label are not confirmed in the available sources.

name: Chile
keyDate: B2C issue since March 2021 mandate; extra recipient and payment data from September 2025
format: DTE XML, digitally signed, SII CAF-stamped
summary: Chile pioneered e-invoicing in 2003 and has required Documentos Tributarios Electrónicos (DTE) for all taxpayers, universally, since 2018. Invoices are XML, digitally signed, and validated with an SII issued CAF (Código de Autorización de Folios) stamp before being forwarded to the buyer; there is no SII provided infrastructure for that forwarding step, unlike some other clearance countries. A December 2024 SII regulation (Resolution 53/2025, effective no earlier than September 2025) added expanded recipient and payment information requirements specifically for B2C electronic receipts (boletas); Exempt Resolution No. 52 of 10 April 2026 postponed enhanced invoice and dispatch guide goods movement data originally set by Resolution 154/2025 until 1 November 2026.

name: China
keyDate: B2B issue since Nationwide from 1 December 2024
format: Fully digitalised e-fapiao (XML data message, QR code)
summary: China completed the nationwide rollout of the fully digitalised e-fapiao on 1 December 2024, following announcements by the State Taxation Administration on 24 November 2024 (Announcement No. 11 [2024], issued 12 November 2024). The system operates on a clearance model through a nationally unified electronic invoice service platform, replacing earlier paper fapiao and regular e-fapiao formats. Digital invoices carry the same legal validity as paper invoices under the Regulations on the Administration of Invoices of the People's Republic of China (Administrative Measures of the People's Republic of China for Invoices).

name: Christmas Island
keyDate: Follows Australia's tax regime — no separate territorial mandate
summary: Christmas Island does not run its own independent tax administration for e-invoicing purposes; it follows Australia's regime directly. Christmas Island's income tax, GST and corporate tax are entirely ATO (Australian Taxation Office) jurisdiction — the local council handles only rates, charges and services, not tax administration. See the Australia dossier for the applicable e-invoicing rules. (Added 10 August 2026 as part of an ISO 3166-1 territory-coverage audit — confirmed case-by-case, not assumed from constitutional status alone.)

name: Cocos (Keeling) Islands
keyDate: Follows Australia's tax regime — no separate territorial mandate
summary: Cocos (Keeling) Islands does not run its own independent tax administration for e-invoicing purposes; it follows Australia's regime directly. Cocos (Keeling) Islands shares the same ATO (Australian Taxation Office) tax framework as Christmas Island and mainland Australia. See the Australia dossier for the applicable e-invoicing rules. (Added 10 August 2026 as part of an ISO 3166-1 territory-coverage audit — confirmed case-by-case, not assumed from constitutional status alone.)

name: Colombia
keyDate: B2B since Preclearance model since January 2019 (largest taxpayers), compulsory for all taxpayers and all transaction types (B2B/B2C/B2G) since November 2020; extended to equivalent documents (payroll, cash register receipts) and ecommerce platforms by Decree 442 of 29 March 2023
format: UBL 2.1, digitally signed, DIAN-issued CUFE clearance code
authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
summary: Colombia's e-invoicing framework, first introduced in 1995 and progressively updated, moved to a mandatory preclearance model in January 2019 (starting with the largest taxpayers) and became compulsory for all VAT-remitting taxpayers and all transaction types (B2B, B2C, B2G) from November 2020. Every invoice must be cleared by DIAN — which issues a CUFE clearance code — before the supplier can send it to the buyer or ship goods. Decree 442 (29 March 2023) extended the framework to equivalent documents (electronic payroll documents, cash register receipts) and required ecommerce platforms to give vendors the means to issue digital sales invoices.

name: Comoros
keyDate: No evidence of any e-invoicing system, VAT regime, or even a standardised national Tax Identification Number system was found in the sources reviewed
model: Not applicable — no e-invoicing model, VAT system, or standardised taxpayer identification infrastructure was confirmed to exist
authority: Direction Générale des Impôts (or equivalent) — exact institutional structure not confirmed in sources reviewed
summary: The Union of the Comoros shows no evidence of an e-invoicing system in the sources reviewed, and the underlying tax administration infrastructure appears considerably less developed than in most other countries covered in this batch. According to IMF-sourced analysis, Comoros does not maintain a formal, standardised, nationwide Tax Identification Number (TIN) system — any taxpayer identifiers that exist are internally assigned, non-standardised, and not publicly verifiable. Formal tax compliance, especially among small businesses, is reported as exceptionally low, with limited taxpayer awareness of registration obligations. Comoros does not operate a formal VAT system, relying instead primarily on indirect and turnover-based taxes. Given the absence of even basic standardised tax administration infrastructure (a working TIN system, a confirmed VAT regime), there is no credible basis for an e-invoicing mandate to exist, and none was found.

name: Cook Islands
keyDate: No mandate
authority: Revenue Management Division (RMD), Ministry of Finance and Economic Management (MFEM), Cook Islands
summary: Cook Islands has no e-invoicing mandate, platform, or published programme as of August 2026. The Revenue Management Division administers tax and customs under the Ministry of Finance and Economic Management, operating an online taxation portal and customs declaration system, but neither authority has announced any e-invoicing requirement or voluntary framework.

name: Costa Rica
keyDate: B2B since general mandate complete 1 Nov 2018; XML v4.4 mandatory 1 Sep 2025
summary: Electronic receipts are universal. Version 4.4 introduced updated technical requirements and has been mandatory since 1 September 2025. Issuers submit signed XML comprobantes to Hacienda for clearance; buyers then confirm acceptance or rejection.

name: Côte d’Ivoire
keyDate: B2B issue since 1 September 2025, phased by tax regime during 2025
summary: Côte d'Ivoire launched the Facture Normalisée Électronique (FNE) clearance platform on 21 July 2025, with nationwide mandatory use for VAT registered taxpayers from 1 September 2025. Invoices (FNE) and retail receipts (RNE) must be prevalidated by the Direction Générale des Impôts before delivery to the customer. By February 2026 more than 52,000 businesses were registered on the platform.

name: Croatia
keyDate: B2B since As of January 1, 2026, Croatia has implemented Fiscalization 2.0
authority: Porezna uprava (Tax Administration), Ministry of Finance
summary: Croatia's "Fiscalization 2.0" reform, effective 1 January 2026, mandates structured e-invoicing (eRačun) for B2B and B2G transactions between VAT-registered businesses, in a Croatia-specific CIUS (HR-FISK 2.0) built on EN 16931. B2C sales require real-time fiscalization reporting to the Tax Administration regardless of payment method, though a traditional receipt (not necessarily a structured e-invoice) is acceptable for the consumer as long as the transaction data is reported. The goal is that essentially every taxable transaction is digitally captured, with very few exceptions.

name: Cyprus
keyDate: B2G receive since 18 April 2020
authority: Ministry of Finance / Treasury of the Republic
summary: Cyprus has implemented the EU Directive 2014/55/EU requirement for public sector bodies to receive and process structured e-invoices compliant with EN 16931, effective April 2019 for central bodies and April 2020 for sub-central bodies. Supplier issuance remains voluntary and the exchange network is Peppol. There is no B2B or B2C mandate and no real-time VAT reporting obligation.

name: Czechia
keyDate: B2B since B2G e-invoice acceptance mandatory since 1 October 2016 (Act No. 134/2016 Sb.); Kontrolní hlášení (VAT Control Statement) e-reporting live since 1 January 2016; B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary, no domestic mandate announced; EU ViDA intra-EU DRR applies from 1 July 2030, national implementation not expected before 2029
model: Post-audit (no CTC/clearance) — invoices exchanged directly between parties; Financial Administration controls ex-post via Kontrolní hlášení cross-matching
format: ISDOC (national UBL 2.0-customised XML, voluntary) for B2B; EN 16931 (UBL 2.1, ISDOC, or EDIFACT syntax) mandatory for B2G acceptance; Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 usable but uncommon
summary: The Czech Republic explicitly operates a post-audit, non-CTC VAT system: the tax authority does not pre-validate or clear invoices, which are exchanged directly between parties. Public contracting authorities have been required to accept EN 16931-compliant e-invoices since 1 October 2016 (Act No. 134/2016 Sb., transposing EU Directive 2014/55/EU), but suppliers have no issuance obligation. Domestically, B2B e-invoicing remains entirely voluntary — Czechia's own national XML format, ISDOC (a UBL 2.0 customisation launched 2008), is built into most Czech ERP/accounting systems, making voluntary structured e-invoicing widespread in practice despite no legal mandate. The core digital-VAT compliance tool is the Kontrolní hlášení (VAT Control Statement), a mandatory transaction-level e-reporting filing live since 1 January 2016, used for ex-post cross-matching of supplier/customer entries to combat carousel/missing-trader fraud — this carries real penalty exposure (CZK 1,000-50,000 fixed fines, up to CZK 500,000 discretionary). Czechia is positioned as an 'aligned follower' on EU ViDA: mandatory intra-EU digital reporting requirements (DRR) apply from 1 July 2030, but no domestic B2B e-invoicing mandate has been announced, with national implementation not expected before 2029. The short-lived real-time sales-reporting system EET was abolished 1 January 2023; a draft 'EET 2.0' law is reported, targeted for 2027, but not enacted.

name: Dominican Republic
keyDate: B2B since Law 32-23 and Decree 587-24 effective 10 October 2024 (DGII Notice 20-24); phased rollout from large national corporations (since May 2023) through medium businesses to small enterprises, closing with smaller taxpayer waves through May 2026; contingency mechanism (Instructivo de Contingencia de FE) published February 2026
model: Post-clearance — electronic invoices (e-CF) sent simultaneously to DGII and the buyer, digitally signed and validated in real time
format: Local XML — electronic tax receipts (e-CF, Comprobante Fiscal Electrónico)
summary: The Dominican Republic's e-invoicing regime is governed by Law 32-23 on Electronic Invoicing and its regulating Decree 587-24, detailed in DGII Notice 20-24, effective from 10 October 2024. The model is a post-clearance system: electronic tax receipts (e-CF), in a locally-defined XML format, must be digitally signed and sent simultaneously to both the DGII (for real-time validation) and the buyer. Rollout has proceeded in phased waves since May 2023, starting with large national corporations, then medium-sized businesses, and closing with small enterprises through May 2026. The law and decree apply to all individuals and entities in the country engaging in transactions involving goods or services, whether paid or free. The DGII provides a free online invoicing tool so SMEs and freelancers can issue compliant e-CFs without needing their own billing software, and published a formal contingency mechanism (Instructivo de Contingencia de FE) in February 2026 to handle technical or connectivity outages.

name: DR Congo
keyDate: B2B issue since Strict compliance 15 May 2026 after a September 2024 pilot and a reported 1 December 2025 mandatory start with grace period
model: Fiscal devices (e-UF / e-MCF) with DGI transmission
summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo fully enforces standardized invoicing (facture normalisée) from 15 May 2026. Taxable persons must issue invoices through DGI connected electronic fiscal devices or approved software, using e-UF where there is no billing system and e-MCF where software already exists, with transmission to the DGI and an official QR code on each validated invoice. VAT may be deducted only against a compliant standardized invoice; sector derogations and case by case relief still exist for some taxpayers.

name: Ecuador
keyDate: B2B issue since Universal 29 November 2022
summary: Electronic receipts are mandatory economy-wide for RUC holders obliged to issue sales receipts. Issuers must create SRI XML vouchers, sign them, and obtain SRI clearance; from 1 January 2026 transmission to the SRI must be immediate. An unauthorized or untransmitted voucher is invalid for IVA input credit and expense deductibility.

name: Egypt
keyDate: B2B receive since from 2023
summary: Egypt operates a fully mandatory clearance-based e-invoicing system supervised by the Egyptian Tax Authority. All VAT-registered businesses must issue JSON or XML invoices cleared in real time through the ETA portal, with paper invoices no longer valid for input VAT recovery or cost deduction as of 2023. B2C electronic receipts continue to roll out in phased waves, with the most recent wave taking effect 15 September 2025 under ETA Resolution No. 281 of 2025.

name: El Salvador
keyDate: B2C issue since only e-tickets to final consumers from 1 January 2025 for taxpayers already in the electronic document regime
model: Clearance (Reception Seal; prior or deferred transmission)
summary: El Salvador's e-invoicing mandate originates from Decree 487/2022, approved by the Asamblea Legislativa on 30 August 2022, reforming the tax code to make Documento Tributario Electrónico (DTE) mandatory, explicitly inspired by e-invoicing regimes already in place in Colombia, Argentina, Peru, and Mexico. The Ministry of Finance estimated approximately 18 months for all sectors to be brought into the mandate following the decree, with waves from 1 July 2023 for large taxpayers and full rollout completed across taxpayer groups in 2024 to 2025. Current technical requirements are governed by the DTE Compliance Regulation (version 1.1, June 2024), which defines ten distinct DTE document types (electronic invoice, tax credit voucher, export invoice, excluded-subject invoice, delivery note, credit note, debit note, settlement voucher, donation voucher, and accounting settlement document); companies may use either prior transmission (document sent to the Tax Authority first, must obtain the Reception Seal before delivery to the customer) or deferred transmission (signed document delivered to the customer first, then sent for validation); electronic signatures must comply with the JWS (JSON Web Signature) standard, and a graphical representation (PDF or similar) must accompany every DTE.

A full B2B mandate is planned for 2027, accompanied by abolition of the EUR 1,000 VAT-reporting threshold, pending final legislation.

name: Eswatini

summary: Eswatini has enacted a legally mandatory e-invoicing and fiscalisation regime: the VAT (Electronic Submission of Fiscal Data and Return-Supporting Records) Notice 2026 under Legal Notice No. 111 of 2026 (in force since 15 July 2026), VAT E-Invoicing Regulations No. 25 of 2026, and the VAT Act (Amendment of Third Schedule) Notice No. 270 of 2026 (in force 3 July 2026), which establish Electronic Fiscal Documents (EFDs). The reform combines B2B e-invoicing, POS fiscal device integration, and real time invoice reporting to ERS, aimed at closing an estimated E4 billion annual VAT compliance gap without raising VAT rates. Rollout is phased by sector, starting with wholesale and retail given their high transaction volumes; ERS began structured stakeholder engagement with that sector in July 2026, so the law is in force but not yet universal and status remains phasing.

name: Ethiopia
keyDate: B2B since Electronic invoicing has been in place since the 2018 Tax Invoice Utilization and Administration Directive No. 149/2018; substantially overhauled by the Electronic Invoice System Administration Directive No. 1142/2026 (issued ~July 2026), a freestanding 31-article clearance-based regime replacing the prior 2-article framework
model: Clearance — every invoice must receive an Invoice Reference Number (IRN), Receipt Reference Number (RRN), and QR code from the Ministry of Revenues' central system before it is legally valid
format: Structured electronic invoice per Ministry of Revenues technical specifications; a sample invoice template is annexed to Directive No. 1142/2026
summary: Ethiopia has operated a clearance-based e-invoicing regime since the Tax Invoice Utilization and Administration Directive No. 149/2018, but the Ministry of Revenues substantially overhauled the framework with the Electronic Invoice System Administration Directive No. 1142/2026 (issued around July 2026), replacing the prior two-article regime with a freestanding, 31-article directive and two technical annexes. Every invoice must now receive an Invoice Reference Number (IRN), Receipt Reference Number (RRN), and QR code from the Ministry's central system before it is legally valid. The new directive introduces multi-track accreditation (separate tracks for system suppliers, SaaS providers, marketplace operators, and exclusive-use developers), mandatory offline resilience for 26 listed business sectors, an Authority-run Cloud Sales Registration System, and manual QR invoices as a last resort, all overseen by a newly established Inspection and Accreditation Board.

name: Falkland Islands
keyDate: No mandate
summary: The Falkland Islands operates its own independent tax administration under the Falkland Islands Government Taxation Office, covering income tax, corporation tax, and related obligations. No e-invoicing mandate, platform, voluntary framework, or published programme has been identified in any official source. The territory remains outside the scope of any e-invoicing requirement as of August 2026.

name: Faroe Islands
keyDate: No mandate
summary: The Faroe Islands is a self-governing territory within the Kingdom of Denmark, outside the EU and Danish VAT area, with its own independent tax authority, TAKS. No e-invoicing mandate, platform, or formal programme has been identified in any of the available sources. The territory operates a highly automated direct-tax withholding system, but this is distinct from any structured e-invoicing obligation.

name: Fiji
keyDate: B2B since VAT Monitoring System (VMS) fiscalisation live since 2017-2018; Phase 3 participants transitioning from VMS v2 to v3, with reaccreditation required by end of 2026
model: Fiscal devices (VMS) — signed receipts issued at point of sale, data transmitted in real time to FRCS via Virtual (V-SDC) or External (E-SDC) Sales Data Controller
summary: Fiji operates the VAT Monitoring System (VMS), a fiscalisation-based e-invoicing regime administered by the Fiji Revenue and Customs Service (FRCS), live since as early as 2017-2018 — among the earliest such systems in the Pacific region. VMS unifies B2C, B2B and B2G transactions: every receipt or invoice is digitally signed and simultaneously transmitted to FRCS, either online via a Virtual Sales Data Controller (V-SDC) or offline via an External Sales Data Controller (E-SDC) with delayed sync, a design suited to a region prone to natural disasters. FRCS, which collects over 85% of government revenue, built the system with Data Tech International (DTI) using the TaxCore platform. All accredited vendors are currently transitioning from VMS version 2 to version 3, with Phase 3 participants required to reaccredit by the end of 2026. Fiji's model has since been adopted regionally, with Samoa (TIMS), Vanuatu (VSMS) and Papua New Guinea (GMS) following the same fiscalisation approach.

name: Finland
keyDate: B2B from EU ViDA mandate expected 1 July 2030
format: EN 16931 (UBL 2.1, CII, Finvoice 3.0, TEAPPSXML 3.0, Peppol BIS Billing 3.0)
summary: Finland enforces mandatory e-invoicing for B2G transactions as of April 2021, under the e-Invoicing Act 241/2019 implementing EU Directive 2014/55/EU. Business buyers with annual turnover above EUR 10,000 may demand structured e-invoices from their suppliers, but there is no general B2B issuance mandate. The EU ViDA reform is expected to introduce mandatory cross-border B2B e-invoicing and digital reporting from 1 July 2030.

name: France
keyDate: B2B issue from 1 September 2027
summary: France is rolling out mandatory B2B e-invoicing in two phases under a Continuous Transaction Controls model. From 1 September 2026, all French VAT registered businesses must be able to receive e-invoices, and large and intermediate sized enterprises must also issue them; SMEs and micro enterprises follow from 1 September 2027. All invoices must flow through government certified Plateformes Agréées (formerly PDPs), which transmit data to the Public Invoicing Portal (PPF) and hence to the DGFiP.

name: French Guiana
keyDate: B2B issue from 1 September 2027
format: Structured electronic invoice via state-accredited platform
summary: French Guiana is a full French département and région d'outre-mer (DROM), fiscally and constitutionally integrated into France. France's national e-invoicing and e-reporting reform therefore applies directly, with all businesses subject to French VAT required to receive electronic invoices by 1 September 2026 and to issue them on a phased schedule extending to 1 September 2027. The reform uses a decentralised 5-corner (Y-model) architecture built around state-accredited platforms (PAs) and the Public Invoice Portal (PPF).

name: French Polynesia
keyDate: No mandate

summary: French Polynesia operates its own independent tax administration, distinct from any parent/host state, but no e-invoicing mandate, platform, or credible programme has been found. French Overseas Collectivity (COM) with its own autonomous tax regime (including its own VAT) — explicitly outside the scope of France's 2026 e-invoicing/e-reporting reform, per that reform's own COM exemption. (Added 10 August 2026 as part of an ISO 3166-1 territory-coverage audit — confirmed case-by-case, not assumed from constitutional status alone.)

name: Gabon
keyDate: B2B since 2026 Finance Law (Loi n°041/2025) makes e-invoicing effective 1 January 2026 for VAT/tax deductibility purposes, with full mandatory enforcement from 1 July 2026 (a 6-month transition period during which customs duty documentation could still substitute)
model: Clearance — standardized electronic invoices (FEN) issued through DGI-approved systems, transmitted to the tax authority for real-time validation and a unique QR code before being legally valid
format: FEN — Facture Électronique Normalisée (standardized electronic invoice); free government e-DEF portal or certified private solutions
summary: Gabon's E-Fact system, established by the 2026 Finance Law (Loi n°041/2025), mandates a standardized electronic invoice (Facture Électronique Normalisée, FEN) for virtually every business transaction — B2B, B2C, B2G, and cross-border — conducted by any person liable to corporate tax, business profits tax, the simplified flat tax, or VAT. The mandate became effective 1 January 2026 for VAT and income-tax deductibility purposes (the FEN, bearing a QR code, is now the only valid invoice format for claiming VAT credits or expense deductions in B2B), with a 6-month transition period during which customs duty documentation could still substitute, ending with full mandatory enforcement from 1 July 2026. Invoices are issued through DGI-approved systems — either the free government e-DEF portal or certified private solutions — and validated in real time with a unique QR code, with invoice issuance itself serving as the e-reporting mechanism. Penalties are severe: fines of up to 100% of the transaction value for failing to issue a compliant e-invoice, with potential business closure for severe infractions.

name: Gambia
keyDate: B2G since Mandatory e-invoicing for VAT proposed in the 2026 Budget Speech (presented to the National Assembly 5 December 2025); Appropriation Act 2026 approved, moving the mandate into an implementation-planning phase; draft Electronic Invoicing Regulations 2025 submitted for stakeholder validation from July 2025 — no live technical requirement or confirmed implementation date yet
model: Not yet confirmed — draft regulations propose a centralized system for receiving electronic invoices
format: Not yet confirmed in sources reviewed
summary: The Gambia has approved, via its 2026 national budget, the introduction of mandatory electronic invoicing for VAT-registered taxpayers, with potential extension to other taxes. The Gambia Revenue Authority (GRA) publicly presented the e-invoicing project on 8 July 2025 and has since worked on draft Electronic Invoicing Regulations 2025, submitted for validation with taxpayer and business stakeholder input. The National Assembly approved the Appropriation Act 2026 (formally passed 9 December 2025), moving the legal mandate for this digital tax transformation into an implementation-planning phase — but as of the sources reviewed, the regulatory framework remains under development, with no confirmed technical requirements, format, platform, or firm implementation timeline published. This is a genuine government-adopted policy commitment (not merely a proposal from an individual official), but it has not yet become an enforceable, technically-specified mandate.

name: Georgia

The Revenue Service operates rs.ge as the taxpayer self service environment, including a linked RS e-invoice system, electronic filing and e-waybill. name: Germany

format: XRechnung or other EN 16931 (ZUGFeRD XRECHNUNG profile accepted at federal level)
summary: Since 1 January 2025 every German-established business must be able to receive structured EN 16931 e-invoices for domestic B2B transactions, with no grace period on the reception side. Mandatory issuance follows a phased timeline: from 1 January 2027 for businesses whose prior-year turnover exceeded €800,000, and from 1 January 2028 for all remaining businesses. E-Reporting for B2B transactions is targeted for July 2030. Germany operates a decentralised model with no central government clearance platform for B2B invoices; exchange occurs directly between trading parties.

name: Ghana

format: TBC: transmitted via GRA's E-VAT/VSDC system; specific schema not confirmed in sources reviewed
summary: The Ghana Revenue Authority operates a phased Electronic VAT Invoicing System (E-VAT), onboarding VAT-registered taxpayers in waves (Phase Two added roughly 2,000 additional taxpayers from September 2024), with invoices cleared in real time through GRA's Virtual Sales Data Controller (VSDC) before issue to customers. Industry reporting describes a broader E-VAT mandate covering all VAT-registered businesses, including non-resident digital platforms, with no revenue threshold, and extending to tax invoices, sales receipts, refunds, credit/debit notes, purchase records, and hospitality statements of account, reported effective from January 2026. A May 2026 industry brief cites 1 July 2026 for all VAT-registered businesses; neither universal date is confirmed on GRA pages in this source set.

name: Gibraltar

summary: Gibraltar has no e-invoicing mandate, platform, or announced programme. The Income Tax Office administers income tax and corporation tax under the Income Tax Act 2010, and has moved to electronic submission of tax returns, but this is distinct from any e-invoicing obligation. Gibraltar has no VAT and is treated as a third country for EU VAT purposes, removing the EU Directive 2014/55/EU framework that drives mandates elsewhere in Europe.

name: Greece

summary: Greece enacted Law 5222/2025 in July 2025, establishing mandatory structured B2B e-invoicing via the myDATA clearance platform. Phase A, covering large enterprises with 2023 revenues above EUR 1 million, became mandatory on 2 March 2026 following a one month postponement, with enforcement from 3 May 2026. Phase B, covering all remaining VAT-registered businesses, begins 1 October 2026 with a transition period to 31 December 2026.

name: Greenland

format: Structured electronic format; secondary sources specify OIOUBL via NemHandel
authority: Government of Greenland (Naalakkersuisut) / Danish Business Authority (NemHandelsRegister)
summary: Greenland has its own independent tax administration (Greenland Tax Agency) and sits outside the EU and Danish VAT area. Mandatory B2G digital invoicing for legal and natural persons supplying goods or services to public authorities has applied since 1 March 2025 under an executive order on digital invoicing published 11 November 2024. Invoices must be issued, sent and received in a structured electronic format that can be processed automatically (exchanged via NemHandel and the NemHandelsRegister); invoices that cannot be processed digitally are rejected. The instrument number of the executive order is still to be confirmed.

The island's 2025 Budget proposal to introduce GST from 2027 is worth monitoring, but nothing in the available sources confirms any e-invoicing obligation or programme linked to that proposal.

name: Hungary
