summary: Hungary's core obligation today is Real-Time Invoice Reporting (RTIR): invoice data for in-scope transactions must be reported to NAV via the Online Invoice System, but the invoice itself can still be paper, PDF, or structured XML — Hungary does not yet require a specific structured e-invoice format for all domestic B2B/B2C invoices. Two additions have layered on: a sector-specific mandatory e-invoicing requirement for electricity/gas supply to non-private customers since 1 July 2025, and a broader receipt data-reporting obligation from 1 September 2026. Separately, NAV has published a conceptual (not yet legislated) framework describing a move to a full ViDA-aligned structured e-invoicing model, in which XML would become the sole legally valid invoice for domestic B2B, cross-border EU B2B, and B2G.

name: Iceland
keyDate: B2G receive since 1 January 2020
format: Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 / UBL 2.1 (TS-236 CIUS, EN 16931)
authority: Ministry of Finance and Economic Affairs; Fjársýsla ríkisins (Financial Management Authority) as Peppol Authority
summary: Iceland has had a mandatory B2G e-invoicing regime since 1 January 2020, requiring all suppliers to public authorities to issue structured electronic invoices compliant with EN 16931 via the Peppol network using Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 or UBL 2.1 under the national CIUS TS-236. The obligation was transposed from EU Directive 2014/55/EU via Regulation 44/2019. There is no B2B or B2C e-invoicing mandate; voluntary adoption in the private sector is growing but remains market-driven.

name: India
keyDate: B2B issue since ₹5 crore threshold from 1 August 2023; first B2B phase was 1 October 2020 for ₹500 crore+
summary: B2B e-invoicing through Invoice Registration Portals is mandatory above ₹5 crore turnover; IRN and QR code are required for validity. Applicability uses aggregate annual turnover in any financial year from 2017-18, and the current ₹5 crore threshold has applied since 1 August 2023.

name: Indonesia
keyDate: B2B issue since 1 July 2016 nationwide (Java and Bali from 1 July 2015)
summary: Indonesia mandates a clearance model of e-invoicing for all VAT-registered businesses via the e-Faktur system, now migrating to the Coretax platform, which is live from 2026 after full enforcement from 31 December 2025. Every VAT invoice must be submitted to the Directorate General of Taxes for real time validation and approval before it is legally valid. Invoices not issued and cleared through the official system are considered invalid for VAT purposes.

name: Iran
keyDate: Moadian system live; precise effective date not confirmed in available sources
summary: Under the Store Terminals and Taxpayers System law, invoices must be issued through the Moadian tax system, a broad CTC regime. The Iranian National Tax Administration (INTA) treats electronic invoicing as a tool for better taxpayer service and voluntary compliance, tackling evasion, economic transparency, tax reporting, and value added tax collection. An INTA journal review still flags B2C control gaps, taxpayer cost and implementation burden, and irregular transactions as challenges.

name: Iraq
keyDate: No mandate published
summary: Iraq has no national tax e-invoicing mandate. The General Commission for Taxes (GCT) administers income tax and related filings, and businesses may issue invoices electronically if counterparties agree. Paper, PDF and other formats remain accepted. Customs digitisation under ASYCUDA requires electronic verification of commercial invoices and certificates of origin for imports from 10 July 2026; that is a border documentation control, not a GCT invoice clearance regime.

name: Ireland
keyDate: B2B from Phase One (large corporates, domestic B2B) 1 November 2028; Phase Two (cross-border EU B2B zero-rate) November 2029; Phase Three (full EU ViDA cross-border) 1 July 2030
model: Structured e-invoicing with real-time data reporting to Revenue (VAT Modernisation programme, aligned with EU ViDA)
format: EN 16931 structured electronic format (e.g. XML) — PDFs and scanned paper documents explicitly excluded
summary: Ireland's Revenue has confirmed a three-phase 'VAT Modernisation' rollout aligned with the EU's VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) initiative. From 1 November 2028 (Phase One), VAT-registered 'large corporates' (those managed by Revenue's Large Corporates Division, established or with a fixed establishment in Ireland) must issue EN 16931-compliant structured e-invoices for domestic B2B transactions and report a subset of invoice data to Revenue in real time; all businesses in Ireland must be able to receive structured e-invoices from that date. Phase Two (November 2029) extends the requirement to VAT-registered businesses involved in cross-border EU B2B trade under zero-rate VAT. Phase Three (1 July 2030) applies full EU ViDA rules to all cross-border EU B2B transactions. Revenue published its implementation plan in October 2025 and confirmed the Phase One large-corporate scope on 10 February 2026.

name: Isle of Man
keyDate: No mandate
authority: Isle of Man Treasury, Income Tax Division
summary: Isle of Man operates its own independent tax administration, distinct from any parent/host state, but no e-invoicing mandate, platform, or credible programme has been found. Crown Dependency with its own Treasury and Income Tax Division; shares a VAT/customs union with the UK under the Common Purse Agreement (unlike Jersey/Guernsey, which are outside the UK VAT area). No e-invoicing mandate found. (Added 10 August 2026 as part of an ISO 3166-1 territory-coverage audit — confirmed case-by-case, not assumed from constitutional status alone.)

name: Italy
keyDate: B2B since 1 January 2019
summary: Italy is Europe's pioneer in mandatory e-invoicing, having required all domestic B2B, B2C and B2G invoices to transit the government's Sistema di Interscambio (SdI) platform in FatturaPA XML format since 2019, with full coverage of all taxpayer sizes achieved on 1 January 2024. The SdI operates as an active clearance hub, validating every invoice against more than 100 formal controls before routing it to the recipient. Italy's authorisation to maintain this domestic mandate runs to 31 December 2027 under EU Council derogation, bridging the period until the ViDA cross-border framework takes effect.

name: Jamaica
keyDate: B2B since Fiscalisation planned; opposition proposal Mar 2026
summary: Tax administration has advanced plans for electronic fiscal solutions; no binding mandate yet. Fiscalisation is planned. In March 2026 the opposition proposed an electronic invoicing system for TAJ that would transmit sales data at the point of sale.

name: Japan
keyDate: recommended standard; no mandate date
format: JP PINT (Peppol BIS Standard Invoice JP PINT)
summary: The Qualified Invoice System (QIS), effective 1 October 2023, changed Japanese Consumption Tax invoice content and issuer registration rules. Structured e-invoicing via Peppol JP PINT is promoted by the Digital Agency and EIPA but remains voluntary; paper and electronic invoices are both valid, with no clearance platform and no transaction level e-reporting. Electronically transacted records must be stored electronically from 1 January 2024 under the e-Bunsho (ERRL) rules.

name: Jersey
keyDate: No mandate
summary: Jersey, a Crown Dependency with its own independent tax administration, has no e-invoicing mandate, clearance platform, or announced programme. Revenue Jersey administers Goods and Services Tax under the Goods and Services Tax (Jersey) Law 2007 and requires GST-registered businesses to issue invoices containing specified fields, but paper and electronic invoices are equally valid provided those fields are present. No pre-approval, real-time transmission, or structured digital format is required.

name: Jordan
keyDate: B2B issue since Phase 2, 1 April 2025
format: XML or JSON, digitally signed and encrypted
authority: ISTD (Income and Sales Tax Department), with the Ministry of Digital Economy and Entrepreneurship
summary: Jordan's JoFotara national e-invoicing platform became mandatory for all VAT-registered taxpayers on 1 April 2025 (Phase 2), covering B2B, B2C and B2G transactions. Invoices are generated in structured XML or JSON, digitally signed and encrypted, and transmitted to ISTD for validation; only invoices processed through JoFotara or an integrated system are valid for tax deduction and accounting purposes.

name: Kazakhstan
keyDate: B2B since Mandatory B2B since 2019 (voluntary from 2014, mandatory for early taxpayer categories from 2017); expanded from 1 January 2026 to cover additional non-VAT-registered sectors
summary: Kazakhstan's Electronic Invoicing Information System (EIIS, also called IS ESF) is a centralised, government-run clearance platform for VAT invoices; direct exchange outside the platform is not permitted. Mandatory for domestic B2B since January 2019 (following a voluntary phase from 2014 and mandatory rollout for early taxpayer categories from 2017), e-invoices are the only valid basis for VAT deduction — paper invoices are not accepted for VAT credit. From 1 January 2026, the mandate expands to cover additional non-VAT-registered sectors, including international couriers, importers, forwarding agents, customs service providers, legal professionals and medical services.

name: Kenya
keyDate: B2B issue since 1 September 2023
summary: Kenya moved from Electronic Tax Registers (ETRs, since 2005) to TIMS (VAT registered taxpayers had to comply by 30 September 2022, extended from 31 July 2022) and then to cloud based eTIMS. The Finance Act 2023 extended eTIMS to all businesses regardless of VAT status from 1 September 2023; from 1 January 2024 only expenses supported by valid eTIMS generated electronic tax invoices qualify for income tax deductions. Kenya uses a clearance model with real time validation through KRA; Reverse Invoicing (self billing) lets approved large buyers invoice on behalf of small scale suppliers in structured chains such as tea and coffee via OSCU/VSCU; non compliance can attract fines of up to KES 1 million, imprisonment of up to three years, or both.

name: Kiribati
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
authority: Ministry of Finance and Economic Development, Kiribati
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Kiribati in the sources reviewed. The Comarch source found for Kiribati is mistagged (content is about Israel's ITA e-invoicing specifications, not Kiribati) and was excluded. No Kiribati-specific evidence was found.

name: Kuwait
keyDate: TBC
summary: Tax reform (including VAT/excise expansion) under discussion; e-invoicing anticipated alongside but not yet legislated.

name: Kyrgyzstan
keyDate: B2B since May 2023 for all taxpayers
summary: Kyrgyzstan requires sales invoices to be registered, issued and received on the State Tax Service ETTN platform. The duty was phased in from May 2022 and, according to STS cited reports, covers all taxpayers from May 2023, with limited patent and single tax exceptions. A commercial guide reviewed in June 2026 said it could not identify a universal B2B mandate, so current STS rules should be reconfirmed.

name: Laos
keyDate: B2B issue since From 1 August 2024
format: Supplier's own template (no mandated structured format confirmed in the sources)
authority: Tax Department, Ministry of Finance (Lao PDR)
summary: Laos introduced VAT and e-invoicing obligations for non-resident digital service and e-commerce providers under Ministry of Finance Instruction 0558/MOF issued in February 2024, effective for transactions from 1 August 2024. Non-resident suppliers must register with the Tax Department, obtain a TIN, and issue e-invoices to B2B customers using their own template, with no mandated structured format specified in the sources. There is no broader domestic B2B or B2G e-invoicing mandate evident from the available sources.

name: Latvia
keyDate: B2B from 1 January 2028
model: Public sector must accept European standard e-invoices (eAddress / latvija.lv)
format: EN 16931 (UBL 2.1 and CII; Peppol BIS Billing 3.0)
authority: VID (Valsts ieņēmumu dienests / State Revenue Service, SRS)
summary: Latvia's e-invoicing rollout, part of its Shadow Economy Curtailment Plan (2024-2027), has B2G e-invoicing mandatory since 1 January 2025, with e-invoice data reporting to the State Revenue Service (SRS) for B2G/G2G transactions mandatory from 1 January 2026 under a Cabinet Regulation dated 9 December 2025. The originally planned 1 January 2026 B2B mandate has been postponed to 1 January 2028, following the Latvian Parliament's adoption of a revised legislative framework in June 2025. Voluntary B2B adoption is encouraged from 2026.

name: Lebanon
keyDate: No mandate announced
summary: Lebanon has no national electronic invoicing mandate. The Ministry of Finance operates electronic declaration and electronic payment services and continues fiscal modernisation projects, but official MoF materials reviewed do not legislate or announce a clearance or interoperability electronic invoicing regime. Paper invoices remain in use, including stamp duty rules on cash invoices and receipts.

name: Lesotho
keyDate: B2B since Value Added Tax (E-Invoicing) Regulations, 2026 came into force 1 April 2026; mandatory go-live for VAT-registered businesses confirmed for 1 August 2026 — already in effect as of this dossier's date (10 August 2026)
model: Clearance-style — every sale, invoice, debit or credit note must pass through an Electronic Billing System (EBS) accredited by Revenue Services Lesotho (RSL), linked to the central Invoice Data Management System (IDMS)
format: Digitally signed invoices with QR code, linked to the central IDMS; specific XML/data schema not detailed in sources reviewed
summary: Lesotho has a mandatory, clearance-style e-invoicing regime that is now live. The Value Added Tax (E-Invoicing) Regulations, 2026 came into force on 1 April 2026, and RSL confirmed 1 August 2026 as the mandatory go-live date for VAT-registered businesses — a date that has already passed as of this dossier. Under the regime, every VAT-registered vendor must issue invoices through an RSL-accredited Electronic Billing System (EBS); each invoice carries a digital signature and QR code linking it to the central Invoice Data Management System (IDMS). The system is not optional — a vendor cannot legally operate without an accredited EBS. Enforcement is strict: administrative penalties range from M50,000 to M300,000, with criminal sanctions of up to M500,000 in fines or six months' imprisonment. Lesotho joins Nigeria, Kenya, Uganda, Egypt, Côte d'Ivoire, Angola and Cameroon among African jurisdictions using clearance-style e-invoicing or continuous transaction controls.

name: Liberia
keyDate: B2B since The Liberia Revenue Authority (LRA) confirmed electronic invoicing is under development as a new feature of its Liberia Integrated Tax Administration System (LITAS), announced at LRA's first Digital Symposium on 15 April 2026 — no confirmed mandatory date, legal basis, or technical specification exists yet
model: Not yet defined — expected to build on LITAS (Liberia Integrated Tax Administration System), which already supports real-time registration, return filing, and payment
summary: Liberia has no e-invoicing mandate yet, but the Liberia Revenue Authority (LRA) has explicitly confirmed that electronic invoicing is under active development. At LRA's first Digital Symposium (Paynesville, 15 April 2026), held as part of Taxpayer Appreciation Month 2026, Assistant Commissioner for the Management Information Systems Division Kollie U. Zayzay stated that new services — including electronic invoicing and VAT features — are being developed within LITAS (Liberia Integrated Tax Administration System), the platform that already allows taxpayers to register, file returns, generate payment slips, and make payments in real time. This builds on a broader digital tax infrastructure that already includes ASYCUDA for customs, electronic fiscal devices monitoring transactions in real time, online tax clearance certificates, and digital verification tools. No confirmed mandatory date, legal basis, or technical specification for e-invoicing itself was identified in the sources reviewed.

name: Libya
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Libya in the sources reviewed. No evidence of a mandate, platform, or proposal was found; sources are generic vendor content and an unrelated tax-disputes article.

name: Liechtenstein
keyDate: B2G receive since ÖAWG of 10 November 2017
model: Interoperability by email; no central platform
authority: Ministry of General Government Affairs and Finance
summary: Liechtenstein has no supplier e-invoicing mandate and no transaction-level CTC or real-time VAT reporting mandate, and no further programme has been announced. Public contracting authorities must accept and process EN 16931 electronic invoices for public procurement contracts above the thresholds in the Public Procurement Act; suppliers are not obliged to issue them. There is no central platform: XML or PDF invoices may be sent by email. We monitor for changes.

name: Lithuania
keyDate: B2B from 1 January 2028 per government plans; not yet enacted
authority: Ministry of the Economy; State Tax Inspectorate (VMI)
summary: Lithuania has operated a mandatory B2G e-invoicing regime since 1 July 2017, delivered through the SABIS platform (which replaced eSąskaita from mid-2024) via the Peppol network and EN 16931-compliant formats. B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary, with no enacted legislation; the government has signalled an intention to introduce a B2B mandate targeting 2028, reusing the SABIS and Peppol infrastructure, but no statute has been published. The i.MAS system (comprising i.SAF, i.VAZ and i.SAF-T) operates as a separate, live digital reporting obligation for VAT and transport data.

name: Luxembourg
keyDate: B2G issue since Phased rollout completed through 2023
authority: AED (Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA)
summary: Luxembourg completed a phased rollout of mandatory B2G e-invoicing through 2023, using the Peppol network and Peppol BIS format, administered by the AED. No domestic B2B or B2C e-invoicing mandate exists beyond that B2G requirement, and no formal fiscalization or real-time reporting system is in place. Luxembourg is expected to await EU ViDA timelines for any future B2B mandate.

name: Macao
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Macao in the sources reviewed. No Macao-specific government source or confirmed mandate was found; all banked content is generic vendor/industry material.

name: Madagascar
keyDate: Waves from 6 months to 2 years after platform implementation
summary: Madagascar has adopted a legal basis for a centralised electronic invoicing system but the platform is not yet live. Decree No. 2025-738 of 2 July 2025 provides for real time transmission and validation of invoices, covering taxpayers who must issue regular invoices (with VAT and without VAT). A pilot will precede size based waves that start only after the platform is implemented; that implementation date is not published in the sources.

name: Malawi
keyDate: B2B issue since 1 May 2026
summary: Malawi has replaced Electronic Fiscal Devices with the Malawi Revenue Authority Electronic Invoicing System. From 1 May 2026 VAT registered businesses must issue tax invoices through EIS, which validates data in real time and returns a unique reference and QR code. By June 2026 MRA reported that 8,260 of about 9,000 targeted VAT businesses had migrated.

name: Malaysia
keyDate: B2C issue since Revenue waves from 1 Aug 2024 through 2026
summary: MyInvois clearance is rolling out in revenue based waves since August 2024, reaching smaller businesses through 2025 to 2026. Micro businesses were originally exempted below RM500,000; in December 2025 the government raised the exemption threshold to RM1 million. An e-Invoice voluntary declaration programme (SVDP) runs until 31 December 2027.

name: Maldives
keyDate: B2B since Mission launched June 2026
summary: The Maldives Inland Revenue Authority has launched an Asian Development Bank funded e-invoicing mission in June 2026 as part of its digital tax administration roadmap. Officials have discussed integrating taxpayer platforms with MIRA systems and have considered a continuous transaction control style model. No legal mandate, invoice format, covered population, or taxpayer obligation date has been published.

name: Mali
keyDate: B2B since No confirmed e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed; the Direction Générale des Impôts (DGI) has a modern digital tax administration (E-Quitus, e-impôt, electronic stamp-duty payment from 1 July 2026) but none of these systems constitute structured e-invoicing
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Mali in the sources reviewed, despite the country's prior 'proposed' classification. Mali's Direction Générale des Impôts (DGI) — recognised as the country's best-digitalised administration during Mali's 2026 Digital Week — operates several genuine digital tax tools: E-Quitus (electronic tax clearance certificates, with a dedicated user manual), e-impôt (an online portal supporting financial-statement submission), and, from 1 July 2026, electronic payment of stamp duty on tax clearance certificates (Instruction N°2026-001/MEF-SG). None of these constitute structured, invoice-level e-invoicing or a Continuous Transaction Control system, and no source described such a system, a specific legislative proposal, or a timeline for one. Given the absence of supporting evidence, this dossier flags the prior 'proposed' status as unconfirmed rather than either fabricating a mandate narrative or unilaterally downgrading it.

name: Malta
keyDate: B2G receive since April 2020 (sub-central; Legal Notices 403 and 404 of 2018 published 30 November 2018)
summary: Public authorities must accept and process EN 16931 e-invoices for public procurement above EU thresholds, under Legal Notices 403 and 404 of 2018 (sub-central receive obligation treated as in place from April 2020). Suppliers are not required to issue e-invoices; B2B and B2C remain voluntary. There is no transaction level CTC or real-time reporting mandate, and no legislated national B2B programme with dates has been published; MTCA has signalled a phased e-invoicing and Digital Real Time Reporting effort aligned with EU ViDA (intra-EU from 1 July 2030). We monitor for changes.

name: Marshall Islands
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
authority: Department of Revenue and Taxation, Ministry of Finance, Banking & Postal Services
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Marshall Islands in the sources reviewed. The official Department of Revenue and Taxation page describes general tax administration functions with no mention of e-invoicing; no mandate, platform, or proposal was found.

name: Martinique
keyDate: Follows France's tax regime — no separate territorial mandate
summary: Martinique does not run its own independent tax administration for e-invoicing purposes; it follows France's regime directly. Martinique is a full French département/région (DROM), fiscally integrated into France. French tax law, including the national e-invoicing/e-reporting reform, applies directly. See the France dossier for the applicable e-invoicing rules. (Added 10 August 2026 as part of an ISO 3166-1 territory-coverage audit — confirmed case-by-case, not assumed from constitutional status alone.)

name: Mauritania
keyDate: Phased rollout announced; no confirmed effective date
summary: Mauritania's Minister of Finance has announced a mandatory e-invoicing regime to be rolled out in phases, beginning with real-time submission of VAT invoices and integration with point-of-sale and ERP systems. The first phase is intended to apply to businesses above a turnover threshold, with a pre-clearance model proposed whereby invoices require tax authority approval before issuance to customers. No confirmed legal instrument, effective date, or technical format standard has been identified in the available sources.

name: Mauritius
keyDate: B2B since VAT e-Invoicing Regulations effective from 2 August 2022; Phase 1 (EBS developer/solution provider registration) live since 26 June 2023; Phase 2 (economic operator onboarding) began in stages from early 2024, initially targeting taxpayers with annual turnover above Rs 100 million; Phase 3 (mandatory issuance) rolling out progressively
model: Fiscalisation/clearance — sellers transmit invoice data via an Electronic Billing System (EBS) to the MRA's Invoice Fiscalisation Platform (IFP) in real time before issuing to the buyer
format: API-based transmission between EBS and IFP; specific document format not confirmed in sources reviewed
summary: Mauritius is introducing a national e-Invoicing system in a phased approach, administered by the Mauritius Revenue Authority (MRA) under Value Added Tax e-Invoicing Regulations effective 2 August 2022 (introduced by the Minister of Finance on 18 September 2023, amended by the Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2022). Providers of goods and services are required to fiscalise their invoices or receipts in real time with the MRA, via an Electronic Billing System (EBS) — the taxpayer's accounting package, invoicing solution, POS, ECR or ERP — connected by API to the MRA's Invoice Fiscalisation Platform (IFP). Phase 1 (software developer/solution provider registration and self-certification) has been live since 26 June 2023. Phase 2 (economic operator onboarding of compliant EBS) began in stages from early 2024, initially targeting taxpayers with annual turnover exceeding Rs 100 million, with further stages extending to smaller taxpayers over time. Phase 3 concerns mandatory issuance of fiscal invoices by economic operators. Each fiscalised invoice receives a unique QR code, enabling customers to independently verify that the transaction was reported to the MRA.

name: Mayotte
keyDate: Follows France's tax regime — no separate territorial mandate
summary: Mayotte does not run its own independent tax administration for e-invoicing purposes; it follows France's regime directly. Mayotte became a full French département/région in 2011, fiscally integrated into France. French tax law, including the national e-invoicing/e-reporting reform, applies directly. See the France dossier for the applicable e-invoicing rules. (Added 10 August 2026 as part of an ISO 3166-1 territory-coverage audit — confirmed case-by-case, not assumed from constitutional status alone.)

name: Mexico
keyDate: B2B issue since Large taxpayers from 2011; all taxpayers from 1 January 2014; CFDI 4.0 exclusive from 1 April 2023
summary: CFDI covers effectively all invoicing, with certified providers (PACs) validating and digitally stamping documents before they reach SAT, among the most comprehensive e-invoicing regimes globally, in force since 2011 with no size or industry exemptions. A 2026 tax reform strengthened authenticity requirements and SAT enforcement powers, and a new Rule 2.9.21 (effective 1 April 2026) goes beyond invoicing itself, requiring digital service providers and marketplace platforms to give SAT direct, real-time access to their transaction data.

name: Micronesia
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
authority: Department of Finance and Administration, Federated States of Micronesia
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Micronesia in the sources reviewed. No government-confirmed mandate, law, or proposal was found; sources are generic vendor/advisory content.

name: Moldova
keyDate: B2B since e-Factura launched as a voluntary system in 2014; B2G mandatory since 2023; cross-border B2B exports added 2025; full mandatory B2B for all VAT-registered domestic transactions from 1 October 2026, following a January 2026 pilot
model: Continuous Transaction Control (CTC) — real-time submission of standardized XML invoices, digitally signed, to the State Tax Service's (SFS) central e-Factura platform
format: Standardized XML via e-Factura, embedded within SIA Cabinetul personal al contribuabilului (the taxpayer cabinet); moving toward Peppol/eDelivery interoperability
authority: State Tax Service (Serviciul Fiscal de Stat, SFS)
summary: Moldova is completing a decade-long transition from voluntary to mandatory e-invoicing via its national e-Factura platform, operated by the State Tax Service (SFS). Launched as a voluntary service in 2014, e-Factura became mandatory for B2G transactions in 2021/2023 (sources vary on the precise year), was extended to cross-border B2B exports in 2025, and will become mandatory for all domestic B2B transactions between VAT-registered entities from 1 October 2026, following a January 2026 pilot phase. The mandate operates as a comprehensive Continuous Transaction Control (CTC) framework: standardized, digitally-signed XML invoices are submitted in real time to the SFS platform, embedded within SIA Cabinetul personal al contribuabilului (the unified taxpayer cabinet) rather than a standalone e-invoicing website. A parallel e-receipt system (eBon, via Virtual Cash Registers) is being introduced for B2C retail transactions. Penalties for non-compliance are severe, ranging up to 25-35% of transaction value. Moldova, an EU candidate country since June 2022, is simultaneously pursuing Peppol/eDelivery interoperability, including EU-supported pilots for Moldova-Ukraine cross-border exchange.

name: Monaco
keyDate: B2B issue from 1 September 2027
authority: Direction des Services Fiscaux (Department of Tax Services)
summary: Monaco shares a single VAT territory with France and, as a result, VAT-registered Monegasque businesses are drawn into France's mandatory electronic invoicing and e-reporting reform. Large and mid-sized enterprises must issue structured e-invoices and transmit e-reporting data from 1 September 2026; all businesses must be capable of receiving them from the same date. Small and micro enterprises gain an additional year, with the issuing obligation extending to them from 1 September 2027.

name: Mongolia
keyDate: B2C issue since eBarimt mandatory nationwide since 1 January 2016
format: Structured electronic receipt via certified POS or software; QR code and unique identifier
summary: The eBarimt system requires electronic receipts and invoices reported to the tax authority economy wide. The mandate has been live nationwide since 1 January 2016 as a real time CTC VAT receipt regime operated by the Mongolian Tax Administration (MTA / GDT). Input VAT credit depends on a matching eBarimt receipt; this is not a Peppol or EN 16931 B2B invoice mandate.

name: Montenegro
keyDate: Not legislated as of July 2026
model: TBC (possible adaptation of Serbia's central platform)
authority: Uprava prihoda i carina Crne Gore
summary: Montenegro requires live real time fiscalisation of invoices issued by VAT registered persons. Invoice data is sent to the Revenue and Customs Administration at issuance and returned with a unique JIKR code plus QR verification. Structured B2B electronic invoicing on a central platform is under discussion and is not legislated as of July 2026.

name: Montserrat
keyDate: No mandate
summary: Montserrat operates an independent tax administration under the Montserrat Customs and Revenue Service, with the Inland Revenue Department administering five direct taxes including income tax, company tax, withholding tax, property tax, and an insurance company levy. No e-invoicing mandate, platform, or credible programme has been identified from the official sources. The department's digital focus as of August 2026 is limited to a property tax online payment platform, with filing tax returns and a property tax calculator listed as coming soon.

name: Morocco
keyDate: B2G since Public consultation launched October 2024; pilot phase from October 2025; mandatory rollout begins early 2026 for ~1,655 large companies (turnover above MAD 200 million); gradual extension to SMEs and micro-businesses in 2027-2028
model: Clearance — invoices must be pre-validated (cleared) by the DGI before being legally valid
authority: Direction Générale des Impôts (DGI) — General Directorate of Taxes
summary: Morocco's e-invoicing mandate is built on Article 145-9 of the General Tax Code (Code Général des Impôts, CGI), introduced via the 2018 Loi de Finances, which provided for electronic handling of invoices and accounting records. The DGI relaunched the initiative with a public consultation in October 2024, ran a pilot phase from October 2025, and mandatory implementation begins in early 2026, per the 2026 Finance Bill (PLF 2026). The first phase covers approximately 1,655 large companies with turnover above MAD 200 million; a gradual extension to SMEs and micro-businesses is planned for 2027-2028. Under the clearance model, every business must issue invoices electronically in UBL 2.1 format and obtain DGI clearance before the invoice is legally valid. xHub, a Moroccan software engineering firm, has been selected as the technology partner developing the national e-invoicing platform. As of the sources reviewed, the government has not yet published a comprehensive implementing decree covering every technical detail (format specifics, electronic signatures, full scope) — these remain subject to further decrees and technical regulations still to be released.

name: Mozambique
keyDate: B2B issue since May 2025 filings (April 2025 transactions)
format: Compressed data file from certified invoicing software
summary: VAT taxpayers must upload a monthly compressed file of invoice data extracted from AT certified invoicing software via the e-declaração platform. That duty has applied since May 2025 under the Tax Authority notice of 27 March 2025 (Notice No. /AT/DGI/2025), which clarifies Article 27(10) of the VAT Code from a 2016 amendment rather than creating a new tax. Certified invoicing software requirements already exist under the Ministerial Order of 29 February 2012; a broader e-invoicing and SAF-T framework remains under preparation.

name: Myanmar
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Myanmar in the sources reviewed. Most banked content is mistagged to Thailand's e-Tax Invoice system (PKF Thailand, Basware Thailand) — excluded as not Myanmar-specific. The one genuine Myanmar source (MPT) is a telecom operator's own billing portal, not a government e-invoicing mandate.

name: Namibia
keyDate: B2B since First announced in the 2024/25 national budget; originally targeted for an April 2026 fixed-date rollout, revised in the 2026/27 budget statement to a phased implementation spanning the 2026/27-2028/29 Medium-Term Expenditure Framework, with no confirmed enforcement dates as of this dossier
model: Planned clearance model — VAT-registered businesses will transmit invoice data to NamRA's Integrated Tax Administration System (ITAS) in near real-time, typically at the point of issuance
format: Not yet published — technical specifications pending
authority: Namibia Revenue Agency (NamRA); Ministry of Finance
summary: As of the most recent detailed briefing (April 2026), Namibia has no mandatory electronic invoicing or e-reporting system in place — all VAT-registered businesses currently issue standard tax invoices (paper or electronic PDF) under existing VAT Act rules, with no centralised clearance or e-reporting platform required. The Namibian government, through the Ministry of Finance and the Namibia Revenue Agency (NamRA), is firmly committed to introducing a comprehensive VAT e-invoicing regime, first announced in the 2024/25 national budget and reaffirmed by NamRA in March 2025 with an initial fixed target of April 2026. The 2026/27 national budget statement officially removed that fixed deadline, repositioning the mandate as part of a broader administrative and tax policy reform package spanning the 2026/27-2028/29 Medium-Term Expenditure Framework — a shift toward a gradual, three-year phased implementation rather than a single-date launch. The future system will operate on a centralised clearance model, requiring VAT-registered businesses (local and foreign) to transmit invoice data to NamRA's Integrated Tax Administration System (ITAS) in near real-time, covering most domestic B2B, B2C (including cash registers), and B2G transactions.

name: Nauru
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
authority: Nauru Revenue Office, Department of Finance
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Nauru in the sources reviewed. The official Nauru Revenue Office page describes general revenue administration with no mention of e-invoicing; no mandate, platform, or proposal was found.

name: Nepal
keyDate: B2B issue since CBMS since 2017; designations expanded over time
summary: Nepal requires designated persons to issue electronic invoices using Inland Revenue Department approved billing software that can link to the Central Billing and Monitoring System (CBMS). The fiscal billing regime has operated since 2017 and, in current commentary, covers taxpayers with turnover above NPR 100 million plus specified cinema, hospitality and internet service providers; other persons may opt in. Tax invoice schedules were amended in 2081 so that invoices must carry HS code, model and brand data.

name: Netherlands
keyDate: B2B since No B2B mandate yet; Ministry of Finance recommended a Peppol-based B2B mandate 10 Mar 2026, draft legislation expected late 2026/2028 depending on source
model: Peppol (market-led); B2B mandate now under active government proposal
format: Peppol BIS (B2G); EN 16931-aligned formats expected for any future B2B mandate
summary: The Netherlands has no domestic B2B e-invoicing mandate today; B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary and requires the buyer's consent. B2G has been mandatory since 2017 (central government) and 2019 (municipalities, provinces, water boards, universities, hospitals and other public bodies), using Peppol. On 10 March 2026 the Dutch Ministry of Finance submitted a parliamentary report recommending a domestic Peppol-based B2B mandate aligned with the EU ViDA framework, moving the country's status from purely voluntary to an active government proposal, though no legislation has been drafted yet.

name: New Caledonia
keyDate: No mandate
authority: Direction des Services Fiscaux, New Caledonia
summary: New Caledonia operates its own independent tax administration, distinct from any parent/host state, but no e-invoicing mandate, platform, or credible programme has been found. French special collectivity with its own autonomous tax regime, including a General Consumption Tax (GCT) distinct from French VAT — explicitly outside the scope of France's 2026 e-invoicing/e-reporting reform, per that reform's own exemption for this collectivity. (Added 10 August 2026 as part of an ISO 3166-1 territory-coverage audit — confirmed case-by-case, not assumed from constitutional status alone.)

name: New Zealand
keyDate: B2G issue from 1 January 2027
summary: From 1 January 2026, government agencies that receive or send more than 2,000 domestic trade invoices a year must be able to send and receive Peppol e-invoices and pay qualifying domestic e-invoices quickly (reported as 95% within five business days). From 1 January 2027 those agencies must require large suppliers (revenue over NZ$33 million in each of the two preceding accounting periods) to submit e-invoices. B2B remains voluntary; there is no economy-wide private sector mandate.

name: Nicaragua
keyDate: Progressive DFE rollout
summary: Nicaragua’s Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) is described as administering an electronic invoicing framework. The most recent secondary source (July 2026) reports a Documento Fiscal Electrónico (DFE) regime whose mandatory adoption is expanding by sector and turnover through DGI administrative dispositions. An October 2025 tracker instead said e-invoicing was not generally allowed except after formal authorization and use of approved software, so taxpayers should confirm their own obligation with DGI.

name: Niger
keyDate: B2B issue since 1 September 2021; remaining SME waves to confirm with the DGI
summary: Niger requires VAT registered taxpayers to issue invoices through the DGI certified electronic invoicing system (SECeF). Each invoice is pre validated and given a unique identifier, a fiscal seal and a QR code before it is a valid tax invoice. Secondary sources date the obligation to 1 September 2021, while a June 2026 guide still advises confirming any remaining SME waves with the DGI.

name: Nigeria
keyDate: B2B issue from Go live 1 July 2027; enforcement January to March 2028 (earlier expectation was 1 January 2026 for small VAT-registered businesses)
format: Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 UBL (XML or JSON)
authority: Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS), formerly Federal Inland Revenue Service (FIRS)
summary: Nigeria's NRS (formerly FIRS) operates the Merchant Buyer Solution (FIRSMBS/MBS) as a Peppol based CTC platform in which structured electronic invoices are generated, validated and transmitted through the national platform. A late 2024 pilot was followed by large taxpayer (annual turnover of NGN 5 billion and above) mandatory B2B and B2G e-invoicing and B2C e-reporting above NGN 50,000 from 1 November 2025, after a 1 August 2025 go live and three month grace period, with enforcement in July 2026. Earlier guidance expected medium and small VAT-registered businesses to become mandatory from 1 January 2026; NRS later set medium taxpayers (NGN 1 billion to NGN 5 billion) to go live on 1 July 2026 with enforcement in January to March 2027, and emerging taxpayers (below NGN 1 billion) to go live on 1 July 2027 with enforcement in 2028. Non-resident suppliers were treated as excluded, with inclusion under consideration for 2026. The legal base includes the FIRS Establishment Act 2007 (Section 25: administer tax laws; Section 26: deploy technology to automate tax processes, assessments and audits) plus the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 and Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025; integration is direct via API or through Accredited Access Point Providers (APPs) authorised under National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) standards, using Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 UBL (XML or JSON).

name: Niue
keyDate: No mandate
authority: Niue Tax Office, Niue Ministry of Finance
summary: Niue has no e-invoicing mandate, platform, or announced programme as of August 2026. The Niue Tax Office administers income tax, PAYE, and the Niue Consumption Tax through an online filing portal, but invoicing itself remains entirely paper or commercially discretionary. No legal instrument, pilot, or policy proposal relating to e-invoicing has been identified in any official source.

name: Norfolk Island
keyDate: Follows Australia's tax regime — no separate territorial mandate
summary: Norfolk Island does not run its own independent tax administration for e-invoicing purposes; it follows Australia's regime directly. Australian tax and superannuation law has applied on Norfolk Island since 1 July 2016, administered directly by the Australian Taxation Office (ATO) — the same authority and framework as mainland Australia, though GST, luxury car tax, wine equalisation tax and fuel tax credits are exempted locally. See the Australia dossier for the applicable e-invoicing rules. (Added 10 August 2026 as part of an ISO 3166-1 territory-coverage audit — confirmed case-by-case, not assumed from constitutional status alone.)

summary: North Macedonia is piloting a national e-Faktura system run by the Public Revenue Office as a centralized, real time clearance platform for non cash invoices. Multi phase testing is underway in 2026, including API work and a taxpayer web application, with a production launch described as following mid 2026. Mandatory use is widely reported for October 2026 (some reports say Q3 2026); later coverage of a draft law describes the system going live on 1 October 2026 and phased mandatory issue and receive for VAT taxpayers from April 2027 (further phase expected July 2027).

name: Northern Mariana Islands
keyDate: No mandate
authority: Division of Revenue and Taxation, Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands
summary: The Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands (CNMI) operates its own tax administration through the Division of Revenue and Taxation, with an income tax system based partly on the US Internal Revenue Code and partly on local CNMI law. No e-invoicing mandate, platform, pilot programme, or credible legislative proposal has been identified in any available official source. The CNMI profile therefore remains at status none as of August 2026.

name: Norway
keyDate: B2B since Stortinget (Parliament) officially approved mandatory B2B e-invoicing legislation June 2026; mandatory issuance from 1 January 2027 (asymmetric — only if buyer is ELMA/Peppol-registered); mandatory reception + automated digital bookkeeping from 1 January 2030
model: Peppol-based exchange, via the EHF format (a Peppol BIS 3.0 implementation aligned with EN 16931); ELMA registry integrated into the Peppol directory
format: EHF (Elektronisk Handelsformat) — Norway's Peppol BIS 3.0 implementation; primary legislation is technologically neutral, requiring only a 'structured, standardized, and machine-readable electronic format'
authority: Skatteetaten / Skattedirektoratet (Norwegian Tax Administration); Ministry of Finance
summary: In June 2026, the Norwegian Parliament (Stortinget) officially approved legislation introducing mandatory B2B e-invoicing and digital bookkeeping, following a March 2026 government letter and a public consultation process. The mandate rolls out in two phases with a deliberately asymmetric structure: from 1 January 2027, all businesses with bookkeeping obligations in Norway must issue e-invoices to any business counterparty registered in the Electronic Recipient Register (ELMA, now integrated into the Peppol directory) — but buyers have no obligation to receive e-invoices until 1 January 2030, when mandatory reception and automated digital-accounting capability also take effect. The practical technical standard will be EHF (Elektronisk Handelsformat), Norway's existing, dominant e-invoice format (89% of e-invoice volume per Norges Bank 2020) — itself a Peppol BIS 3.0 implementation fully aligned with EN 16931 — though the primary legislation itself remains technology-neutral. Exemptions are planned for micro-businesses under NOK 50,000 annual turnover and specific regulated sectors (bankruptcy estates, financial enterprises, banks, insurers, pension funds). The bill still requires Royal Assent, and Skattedirektoratet must publish detailed technical regulations (forskrift) by 15 December 2026 at the latest.

name: Oman
keyDate: B2B issue from 1 April 2027
summary: The Fawtara programme is the Oman Tax Authority VAT e-invoicing regime, announced with a phased rollout from late 2026 into 2027 starting with large taxpayers. Decision No. 189/2026 sets mandatory electronic tax invoices from 1 April 2027 for VAT taxable persons with annual supplies above OMR 5 million, and from 1 October 2027 for those at or below that threshold, after a voluntary pilot of 100 selected companies from the end of August 2026. Exchange is planned on a Peppol five corner model through licensed service providers; specifications and accreditation remain in development.

name: Pakistan
keyDate: B2C issue since Notification dated 19 February 2026; a later commencement date is not stated
summary: Pakistan operates a mandatory centralised clearance e-invoicing system administered by the Federal Board of Revenue, under which notified taxpayers must integrate their ERP or POS systems with the FBR IRIS platform via licensed integrators for real-time invoice validation. The rollout is phased by taxpayer category and turnover, with large retailers mandated to link their invoicing systems with FBR by December 1. Each validated invoice receives a unique Invoice Reference Number, UUID, and QR code from the FBR before it may be legally issued.

name: Panama
keyDate: B2B issue since 1 March 2024
summary: Panama operates the Sistema de Factura Electrónica de Panamá (SFEP), under which taxpayers must issue digitally signed XML invoices (Comprobantes Fiscales Electrónicos) validated and authorised in real time by a DGI certified provider known as a PAC. The legal framework rests primarily on Law 256 of 2021 and Executive Decree 766 of 2020, with subsequent resolutions progressively expanding the mandatory scope to cover most taxpayers. From 1 January 2026, only taxpayers with annual gross revenues up to B/. 36,000 and issuing no more than 100 documents per month may use the DGI free invoicing tool; all others must use a certified PAC.

name: Papua New Guinea
keyDate: No national mandate
summary: Papua New Guinea has no national electronic invoicing mandate. The Internal Revenue Commission administers GST and other taxes and has digitised some filing and payment through myIRC, but invoices remain conventional tax documents. Sources describe GST content and seven year record keeping, not a clearance platform, mandated syntax, or go live date.

name: Paraguay
keyDate: B2G issue since From 2 January 2026
summary: Paraguay is phasing mandatory electronic tax documents (DTEs) through SIFEN under the DNIT. Designated taxpayer groups must issue signed XML via e-Kuatia or e-Kuatia'i; General Resolution 21/2024 covers groups 11 to 18 from 3 March 2025 to 1 December 2026, and General Resolution DNIT No. 52 adds groups 19 to 24 through 1 September 2027. New legal entities in the RUC have been electronic only since 1 April 2025, and state suppliers since 2 January 2026, except the Virtual Withholding Voucher.

name: Peru
keyDate: B2B since Universal across remaining taxpayer segments from 1 June 2022; Resolution 000075-2026 effective 1 June 2026 for new registrations and regime changes
summary: Peru's Comprobante de Pago Electrónico (CPE) system is mandatory across taxpayer segments via SUNAT's Electronic Issuance System (SEE) or authorised Electronic Service Operators (OSE). SUNAT Resolution No. 000075-2026, effective 1 June 2026, ties the start of mandatory e-invoicing to the date of RUC (taxpayer registry) registration for certain tax regimes, and to regime-exit dates for others, while expanding Integrated Electronic Records System (SIRE) obligations. A subsequent update postponed the SIRE deadline for Principal Taxpayers (PRICOS) from June 2026 to October 2026.

name: Philippines
keyDate: B2B issue from enforceable issuance 31 December 2026 (Stage 1 rollout began March 2026; original date 14 March 2026)
model: Structured e-reporting (not clearance); buyer delivery unregulated
summary: The BIR Electronic Invoicing System (EIS) is mandated by Revenue Regulation No. 11-2025 (25 February 2025). Stage 1 rollout began March 2026 for large taxpayers, e-commerce and digital platforms, with the enforceable issuance obligation extended to 31 December 2026 by RR No. 26-2025; the BIR has clarified that electronic sales reporting follows later under Section 237-A once its system is ready. Stage 2 (exporters, incentivized enterprises, POS retailers) is expected later in 2027 and is BIR readiness dependent.

name: Pitcairn Islands
keyDate: No mandate
authority: Government of the Pitcairn Islands (Island Council)
summary: Pitcairn Islands is a British Overseas Territory with a resident population of approximately fifty people. No e-invoicing mandate, platform, programme, or legislative framework relating to electronic invoicing has been identified in any available official source. The territory's administrative scale makes a formal e-invoicing regime neither present nor foreseeable.

name: Poland
keyDate: B2B issue from January 2027
format: EN 16931 (UBL 2.1 and CII); Peppol BIS Billing 3.0
summary: KSeF became mandatory on 1 February 2026 for large taxpayers (annual revenue above PLN 200 million) and on 1 April 2026 for other VAT-registered businesses; micro-entrepreneurs follow January 2027. Invoices must be accepted by the KSeF platform to be valid. Penalties are suspended until 2027.

name: Portugal
keyDate: B2B from B2G live (CIUS-PT); B2B/B2C not mandated for structured e-invoicing. QES requirement for PDF invoices delayed to 1 January 2027; SAF-T submission delayed to 2028
summary: Portugal mandates B2G e-invoicing in CIUS-PT format, and requires an ATCUD code (via certified software) and QR code on invoices generally, but domestic B2B/B2C structured e-invoicing remains voluntary. Two separate, long-delayed obligations continue to slip: the Qualified Electronic Signature (QES) requirement for PDF invoices, originally due 1 July 2021, has been postponed repeatedly and now takes effect 1 January 2027 (per law 37/XVII/1, voted December 2025); mandatory SAF-T file submission, originally set for 2026, has similarly slipped to 2028.

name: Puerto Rico
keyDate: No mandate
authority: Departamento de Hacienda de Puerto Rico
summary: Puerto Rico operates its own independent tax administration under the Departamento de Hacienda and levies a Sales and Use Tax (IVU) at a combined rate of 11.5 percent, administered digitally through the SURI portal. No e-invoicing mandate, structured B2B or B2G e-invoicing programme, or credible announcement of one has been identified in the available sources. The SURI portal obligation covers tax-return filing and merchant registration, not structured invoice exchange between trading parties.

name: Qatar
keyDate: No mandatory go-live date officially published
summary: On 6 May 2026 Qatar's Cabinet approved a draft e-invoicing law and executive regulations prepared by the Ministry of Finance and the General Tax Authority (GTA). E-invoicing is part of tax digitalisation and is expected to follow GCC peers, but there is still no published mandate and GTA has not issued a model, format, scope or official go-live date. The draft must complete the legislative process; treat implementation as forthcoming and unconfirmed.

name: Republic of the Congo
keyDate: B2C issue since First phase
summary: The Republic of the Congo is phasing in a Certified Electronic Invoicing System (SFEC). The first phase takes effect from 1 August 2026 for large enterprises (UGE), medium-sized enterprises (UME), oil and gas subcontractors (USTPG), and all suppliers of goods and services to those entities. Invoices must be certified electronically in real time via API or, as a temporary fallback, the eFacture platform; later waves and the invoice syntax are not confirmed in the sources.

name: Réunion
keyDate: Follows France's tax regime — no separate territorial mandate
summary: Réunion does not run its own independent tax administration for e-invoicing purposes; it follows France's regime directly. Réunion is a full French département/région (DROM), fiscally integrated into France. French tax law, including the national e-invoicing/e-reporting reform, applies directly. See the France dossier for the applicable e-invoicing rules. (Added 10 August 2026 as part of an ISO 3166-1 territory-coverage audit — confirmed case-by-case, not assumed from constitutional status alone.)

name: Romania
keyDate: B2B since B2G since 2016; B2B mandatory since July 2024; B2C mandatory via RO e-Factura since January 2025; unified 5-working-day transmission deadline from January 2026
summary: All domestic B2B invoices in Romania flow through the RO e-Factura clearance platform, mandatory since July 2024, with B2C reporting added via the same system from January 2025. Government Emergency Ordinance 89/2025 (23 December 2025) unified the transmission deadline for both B2B and B2C invoices to 5 working days from January 2026 (previously 5 calendar days for B2B, undefined for B2C), clarified that B2B invoices to non-established-but-VAT-identified buyers must still route through RO e-Factura, and introduced a new registration requirement for individual entrepreneurs (using their personal CNP identifier) before starting economic activity.

name: Russia
keyDate: B2G since 1 April 2024
summary: Russia operates a live e-invoicing regime anchored by the Universal Transfer Document (UPD) and a network of FNS-accredited Electronic Document Management operators. E-invoicing is mandatory for taxpayers dealing in traceable goods (from 1 July 2021) and for federal government contract supply (from 1 April 2024), while general B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary but is heavily adopted. Plans to extend a full mandatory B2B mandate were suspended by the Ministry of Finance in June 2022 and no new target date is confirmed in the available sources.

name: Rwanda
keyDate: B2B issue since 1 January 2021
summary: Electronic Billing Machines and certified invoicing software (EBM) are mandatory for VAT registered businesses and, under the 2023 tax procedures law, for every person carrying out taxable activities. Invoices must be issued on every sale, with data sent to the Rwanda Revenue Authority. The Electronic Invoicing System has been mandatory since 1 January 2021.

name: Saint Barthélemy

summary: Saint Barthélemy is a French Overseas Collectivity (COM) with its own autonomous tax code, entirely separate from metropolitan France's tax jurisdiction. France's national B2B e-invoicing reform, phasing from September 2026, does not extend to Saint Barthélemy.

summary: San Marino has no domestic e-invoicing mandate requiring electronic invoicing between San Marino operators. However, a live mandatory framework governs cross-border electronic invoicing in trade in goods and services between San Marino and Italy, using Italy's SDI infrastructure with an additional San Marino Tax Office layer. The legal basis is Delegated Decree No. 163 of 20 September 2021 and supporting regulation.

name: Saudi Arabia
keyDate: B2B issue since waves from 1 Jan 2023; Wave 25 by 1 Feb 2027
model: Generation (structured e-invoice; no Fatoora clearance in Phase 1)
summary: Saudi Arabia FATOORA e-invoicing is fully operational under ZATCA. Phase 1 has required all resident VAT registered taxpayers to generate structured electronic invoices since December 2021 (4 December 2021). Phase 2, live from 1 January 2023 in over 24 revenue based waves, adds mandatory API integration with the FATOORA platform for real time B2B/B2G clearance and 24 hour B2C reporting; Wave 24 used a SAR 375,000 threshold, and Wave 25 requires integration by 1 February 2027 for VAT subject revenue above SAR 187,500 in any of 2022 to 2025.

name: Senegal
keyDate: B2B since 2025 Finance Bill ends the voluntary status e-invoicing has held since 2008, making electronic invoicing mandatory for all taxable entities; no official implementation timeline had been released as of the sources reviewed
model: Not yet finalised — invoices must be submitted in a structured electronic format via either a public invoicing portal or another authority-designated digital platform; exact format and platform not yet specified
format: Structured electronic format — specific standard not yet specified; Benin's e-MECeF (structured JSON files to a centralised platform) referenced as a potential model
authority: Direction Générale des Impôts et des Domaines (DGID)
summary: Senegal's Directorate General of Taxes and Domains (DGID) is transitioning e-invoicing from a voluntary option (permitted since 2008 under the General Tax Code but never centrally systemised, resulting in limited adoption) to a mandatory regime, via the 2025 Finance Bill. The new legislation applies to all taxable entities and requires invoices to be submitted in a structured electronic format through either a public invoicing portal or another digital platform designated by the authorities; the exact technical format has not been specified, though Senegal has looked to neighbouring Benin's e-MECeF system (structured JSON files to a centralised platform) as a potential model. Non-compliance — failing to issue, transmit, or receive electronic invoices — carries fines of 25% of the VAT that should have been invoiced electronically, capped at XOF 5 million (approximately EUR 7,700) per invoice. No official implementation timeline had been released as of the sources reviewed.

name: Serbia
keyDate: B2B since 1 January 2023
summary: Serbia rolled out mandatory e-invoicing in three phases via the national SEF (Sistem e Faktura) platform: public sector suppliers had to issue e-invoices to government from 1 May 2022, public entities had to be able to send e-invoices to companies from 1 July 2022, and B2B e-invoicing became mandatory economy-wide from 1 January 2023. Non-compliance carries a fine of around €17,000; invoices are stored via the ancillary Sistem za Upravljanje Fakturama (SUF). Serbia has postponed key SEF B2B e-invoicing reforms until the end of 2026, allowing more time for businesses to adapt to expanded requirements, electronic archiving, and stricter VAT reporting. Later amendments (Official Gazette 109/2025 and E-Invoicing Rulebook 30/2026) refine SEF VAT recording from the April 2026 tax period, and from 1 July 2026 all e-invoices to public sector recipients must be registered in the Central Invoice Register (CRF).

name: Seychelles
keyDate: B2G since Cabinet approved introduction of an electronic invoicing system (announced 8 February 2024); procurement formally began March 2026 with publication of an Expression of Interest; Seychelles Revenue Commission (SRC) entered the final stage of e-invoicing procurement as of 25 July 2026 — system not yet implemented
model: Automatic real-time transfer of billing information between businesses and the tax authority (per Cabinet's description); technical model not yet finalised pending procurement outcome
format: Not yet confirmed — pending procurement of the Electronic Invoicing Solution (EIS)
summary: Seychelles has a Cabinet-approved plan for mandatory electronic invoicing, first announced in February 2024 as part of budget reforms to improve tax compliance and reduce revenue leakage, initially covering VAT with other taxes to be added in stages. The Seychelles Revenue Commission (SRC) issued a formal Expression of Interest for a 'Consultancy Services for the Supply and Implementation of an Electronic Invoicing Solution (EIS)' with a December 2025 submission deadline, and as of 25 July 2026 SRC confirmed it has entered the final stage of procurement — but the system itself has not yet been implemented. This is a genuine, government-committed initiative moving through a lengthy but real procurement pipeline, not yet a live or technically-specified mandate.
