name: Singapore
keyDate: B2G issue since 1 November 2008
format: Peppol PINT SG (replacing SG Peppol BIS Billing 3.0)
summary: Singapore is phasing in mandatory GST invoice data transmission via the InvoiceNow network (Peppol based). The GST InvoiceNow Requirement applies progressively: newly incorporated voluntary GST registrants from 1 November 2025, all new voluntary GST registrants from 1 April 2026, and all remaining GST registered businesses in waves from April 2028 through April 2031. B2B e-invoicing itself is not universally mandated; the obligation is specifically to transmit invoice data to IRAS through InvoiceNow-Ready Solutions using the Peppol PINT SG format.

name: Sint Maarten
keyDate: No mandate
authority: Tax Administration Sint Maarten (Inspectorate of Taxes)
summary: Sint Maarten operates its own independent tax administration established on 10 October 2010, when the island became a constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands. No e-invoicing mandate, structured format requirement, or credible legislative programme has been identified in the available sources. Invoicing obligations exist within the Turnover Tax (TOT) framework, but no electronic invoice format or clearance model has been introduced.

name: Slovakia
keyDate: B2B issue from 1 January 2027
authority: Financial Administration of the Slovak Republic (Finančná správa SR)
summary: Slovakia has a live B2G e-invoicing mandate via the IS EFA platform and is introducing a mandatory B2B e-invoicing and real-time reporting obligation from 1 January 2027, with a proposed penalty-free grace period through 31 March 2027. The B2B system is built on a 5-corner Peppol network operated by accredited Digital Postmen, requiring EN 16931-compliant structured XML invoices; a voluntary pilot opened from Q2 2026. Reporting of purchase invoices has been proposed to be deferred to 1 July 2030, aligned with the EU ViDA initiative.

name: Slovenia
keyDate: B2B from 1 January 2028
format: e-SLOG 2.0, UBL 2.1, UN/CEFACT CII, Peppol BIS 3.0
authority: Financial Administration of the Republic of Slovenia (FURS); Ministry of Finance
summary: Slovenia has required B2G e-invoicing via the e-SLOG standard since 2015, processed through the Public Payments Administration (UJP/PPA). On 23 October 2025 the National Assembly adopted the Act on the Exchange of Electronic Invoices and Other Electronic Documents (ZIERDED), promulgated by the President on 31 October 2025, setting 1 January 2027 as the definitive B2B mandate date (postponed from a January 2027 draft target, itself postponed from earlier April/July 2026 proposals). The final law uses a Decentralized Continuous Control and Exchange Model (DCTCE) and removed the real-time e-reporting obligation that appeared in draft bills; accepted formats are e-SLOG 2.0, Peppol BIS 3.0, UBL 2.1, or EN 16931 CII.

name: Solomon Islands
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Solomon Islands in the sources reviewed. Only one source was found for this country, a directory stub with no substantive content. No evidence of a mandate, platform, or proposal exists.

name: Somalia
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Somalia in the sources reviewed. No SRA-specific mandate, law, or proposal was found; sources are generic directory/vendor content.

name: South Africa
keyDate: B2B since SARS has confirmed mandatory e-invoicing targeted for 2028 under the VAT Modernisation Project; Draft Tax Administration Laws Amendment Bill (TALAB) published for comment 16 August-12 September 2025; large taxpayers first, phased over five years from an initial 2023 proposal
model: Anticipated decentralised Five-Corner Model (Peppol-style, via approved/certified service providers) — not yet legislated in final form
format: TBC — structured electronic format (e.g. XML); PINT (Peppol International Invoice) under consideration; final technical specification not yet published
authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); National Treasury
summary: South Africa does not yet mandate e-invoicing. Under its VAT Modernisation Project, SARS published a discussion paper in September 2023 proposing a shift to real-time VAT reporting (invoice/payment data submitted within 24 hours, eventually reduced to 6 then 1 hour, using submitted data to pre-populate VAT returns, phased over five years starting with large taxpayers). SARS and National Treasury published the Draft Tax Administration Laws Amendment Bill (TALAB) for public comment from 16 August to 12 September 2025, laying the legal groundwork for mandatory e-invoicing and e-reporting. SARS has since confirmed a target of 2028 for mandatory e-invoicing, with South Africa reportedly leaning toward a decentralised Five-Corner (Peppol-style) model similar to France, Singapore and Belgium, potentially using the PINT (Peppol International Invoice) format. Since 1 April 2025, invoice data has also been required on electronic customs declarations, and companies wishing to use EDI-based invoicing today still need prior SARS/National Treasury authorisation.

name: South Korea
keyDate: B2B issue since 1 January 2011
format: e-Tax Invoice XML with PKI digital signature
summary: South Korea's e-Tax Invoice (전자세금계산서) system, one of the world's earliest e-invoicing mandates, has required all corporate taxpayers to issue and transmit electronic tax invoices to the NTS Hometax platform within one day of issuance since 1 January 2011. The mandate has progressively extended to individual entrepreneurs (sole proprietors) via a steadily lowered annual turnover threshold, currently 80 million KRW as of July 2024, with a further reduction from July 2025. Invoices must be PKI digitally signed XML, archived for 5 years; late or missing transmission triggers automatic penalties, typically 0.5% of the supply value.

name: South Sudan
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for South Sudan in the sources reviewed. NRA's eTax platform is a general Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) registration and online filing system, not a structured e-invoicing mandate — no e-invoicing-specific evidence was found. (Note: this is a distinct country from Sudan, which has a genuine, separate e-invoicing rollout covered in its own dossier.)

name: Spain
keyDate: B2B from 1 October 2027 if the Ministerial Order enters into force on 1 October 2026
format: Facturae (qualified certificate electronic signature); EN 16931 accepted by public authorities
summary: Spain has a live B2G e-invoicing mandate in place since January 2015, requiring structured Facturae invoices via the FACe platform. The B2B mandate under Law 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) was given legal force by Royal Decree 238/2026, published in March 2026, with a draft Ministerial Order setting an expected entry into force date of 1 October 2026 that would trigger compliance deadlines of 1 October 2027 for large businesses and 1 October 2028 for all remaining in scope taxpayers. The Spain 2025 EC Country Sheet carries a NO VERIFICATION status, so the B2B mandate fields in that source have not been officially validated by Spanish national representatives.

name: Sri Lanka
keyDate: B2B issue since Tea brokers from 1 May 2026; full Phase 1 Web API by end of 2026
format: VAT Schedules 01, 04 and 07 via RAMIS Web API
summary: Sri Lanka has moved beyond a study phase: Budget 2026 announced a National e-Invoicing System and IRD Notice SEC/PN/VAT/2026-03 (4 May 2026) describes a Web API that sends VAT invoice schedule data from ERP systems to RAMIS. Selected export sectors are already connected; tea brokers have transmitted invoice, credit note and debit note records from 1 May 2026, with Phase 1 (VAT registered export oriented enterprises) targeting full Web API integration by the end of 2026 and Phase 2 later covering all VAT registered persons. A general e-invoicing mandate has not been found in the VAT Act or IRD gazette texts reviewed; the live obligation is the IRD notice and the phased pilot, not a legislated countrywide mandate.

name: St. Kitts & Nevis
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
authority: Inland Revenue Department, St. Kitts & Nevis
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for St. Kitts & Nevis in the sources reviewed. Official government sources confirm active VAT administration (rate changes, digital entry systems) but no e-invoicing-specific mandate, platform, or proposal.

name: St. Lucia
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for St. Lucia in the sources reviewed. The official VAT Act section governs traditional (paper) tax invoices and sales receipts, with no electronic invoicing provisions found.

name: St. Vincent & the Grenadines
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
authority: Inland Revenue Department, St. Vincent & the Grenadines
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for St. Vincent & the Grenadines in the sources reviewed. Multiple official government sources were found, confirming active digital-government initiatives (e-payment platform, customs, IRD online services), but none describe a structured e-invoicing mandate or platform.

name: Sudan
keyDate: B2B issue since beginning of May 2026
model: Clearance (real time submission to the Taxation Chamber)
summary: Sudan's Taxation Chamber launched its electronic invoice system in May 2026, with invoice information sent in real time to the tax authority. The chamber agreed a timetable with the Ministry of Finance to fully computerise the system by the end of 2026 and set a target of 2,000 taxpayers on electronic invoicing. Legal instrument names, turnover thresholds, and the technical format are not confirmed in the available sources.

name: Suriname
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Suriname in the sources reviewed. No Suriname-specific mandate, platform, or proposal was found in the sources reviewed.

name: Svalbard & Jan Mayen
keyDate: No mandate
authority: Norwegian Tax Administration (Skatteetaten), Svalbard Tax Office
summary: Svalbard and Jan Mayen have no e-invoicing mandate, platform, or credible programme. Svalbard operates under its own simplified flat-tax regime with no VAT, administered by the Svalbard Tax Office under rules distinct from mainland Norway; Jan Mayen applies mainland Norwegian tax rates but has no permanent population. The mainland Norwegian B2B e-invoicing mandate announced for 1 January 2027 applies to entities subject to Norwegian bookkeeping requirements on the mainland and does not extend to Svalbard or Jan Mayen.

name: Sweden
keyDate: B2G issue since 1 April 2019
authority: Skatteverket / DIGG (Peppol authority transferring to Upphandlingsmyndigheten from Jul 2026)
summary: Sweden has a live B2G e-invoicing mandate covering central government agencies since 2008, and all public procurement contracts since 2019, with suppliers required to issue EN 16931-compliant invoices and all contracting authorities required to receive them via the Peppol network. B2B e-invoicing remains voluntary but is widely practised. A formal government inquiry launched in February 2026 will assess whether domestic B2B e-invoicing and digital reporting requirements should be introduced, with findings due no later than November 2027.

name: Switzerland
keyDate: B2B since B2G e-invoicing mandatory since 1 January 2016 for federal contracts ≥ CHF 5,000; B2B and B2C e-invoicing remain voluntary as of 2026, with no domestic B2B mandate planned — Swiss exporters are instead being pulled into structured invoicing indirectly by France's (from 1 September 2026) and Germany's (from 2027) mandates
model: B2G: pre-clearance-style submission to the Federal Tax Administration via certified providers (no central government portal). B2B/B2C: voluntary, no clearance model
format: SwissDIGIN (Swiss standard); ZUGFeRD/Factur-X (hybrid format) recommended; UBL XML, eCH-011, and Peppol BIS also accepted; QR-bill mandatory for payment slips
summary: Switzerland has no domestic B2B or B2C e-invoicing mandate; both remain fully voluntary, and Swiss law's only standing structured-invoicing obligation is for B2G transactions: since 1 January 2016, suppliers billing the federal administration for contracts of CHF 5,000 or more must submit electronic invoices, via certified service providers rather than a central government portal. Switzerland's own recommended standard is SwissDIGIN, with the hybrid ZUGFeRD/Factur-X format also recommended and UBL XML, eCH-011, and Peppol BIS accepted. Separately, and distinct from invoice-level e-invoicing, the QR-bill is the mandatory format for Swiss payment slips (replacing the old payment slip), continuing to evolve technically (structured-address-only requirement from 21 November 2025, implementation guidelines version 2.4). As of 2026, no domestic B2B mandate is planned, but Swiss exporters selling into the EU are being pulled toward structured invoicing indirectly, since France requires structured B2B e-invoicing from 1 September 2026 and Germany from 2027 — EU customers will increasingly refuse PDF invoices regardless of Swiss domestic law.

name: Syria
keyDate: B2G since In March 2026, Syria's tax authority discussed reforms covering a unified income tax, sales tax, real-estate sales tax and stamp duty, together with electronic invoicing and electronic payment; in April 2026, a proposed invoicing platform linking companies to the Ministry of Finance through the tax number and commercial register was presented — no enacted law, technical specification, or implementation date exists
model: Not yet confirmed — proposed platform would link companies to the Ministry of Finance via tax number and commercial register
format: Not yet confirmed in sources reviewed
authority: Syrian Ministry of Finance / General Commission for Taxes and Fees
summary: Syria has no enacted e-invoicing system, but there is genuine, recent evidence of active government discussion and proposal. In March 2026, Syria's tax authority discussed a package of reforms including a unified income tax, sales tax, real-estate sales tax, stamp duty, electronic invoicing, and electronic payment; in April 2026, a proposed invoicing platform linking companies to the Ministry of Finance via their tax number and commercial register was presented. This is distinct from vendor marketing pages (such as tax2gov's 'STA E-Invoicing API' page) which speculatively describe what a future system 'would' look like while explicitly confirming 'the Syrian Tax Authority (STA) has no formal e-invoicing system as of 2025 due to ongoing instability.' Given the genuine but very recent and unformalised nature of the April 2026 proposal, this is classified as 'proposed' rather than 'announced' or 'none'.

name: Taiwan
keyDate: B2B since eGUI mandatory for all taxpayers since 2018-2021 rollout; MIG 4.0 XML standard mandatory since 1 January 2024 (MIG 3.1/3.2 usable only through 31 Dec 2025); Electronic Invoice Allowance Note (EIAN) reporting rules effective 1 January 2025, fully enforced since 30 June 2025
model: Government platform (electronic Government Uniform Invoice — eGUI), real-time/near-real-time digital reporting
format: eGUI XML (MIG 4.0 since 1 Jan 2024, superseding MIG 3.1/3.2.1), plus a QR-coded PDF
authority: Ministry of Finance (MOF), National Taxation Bureau of Taipei
summary: Taiwan's electronic Government Uniform Invoice (eGUI) scheme has roots in a 2006 standardisation programme; the Ministry of Finance imposed mandatory e-invoicing via gradual implementation from 2018, extending to all taxpayers by January 2021 (foreign and national companies alike), operated through the MOF's Electronic Invoicing Platform. The technical standard was upgraded to MIG 4.0 XML, mandatory from 1 January 2024 (older MIG 3.1/3.2 versions usable only through 31 December 2025). Since 1 January 2025, new rules require sellers to issue and upload an Electronic Invoice Allowance Note (EIAN) for returns, withdrawals, or agreed discounts, with strict upload deadlines (2 days for B2C, 7 days for B2B from the day after issuance); a transitional period ended 30 June 2025, after which full enforcement began, with penalties of NT$1,500-15,000 for late or inaccurate uploads.

name: Tajikistan
keyDate: VAT e-invoices accepted via electronic cabinet
summary: Electronic VAT invoices can be used through the Tax Committee state system (the taxpayer electronic cabinet) and annexed to VAT returns. They are accepted for VAT payers but are not confirmed mandatory; paper remains valid. An older classification treated electronic VAT invoicing through the state system as required for VAT payers.

name: Tanzania
keyDate: B2B since EFD Phase 1 (VAT-registered traders) since 2010; Phase 2 (non-VAT traders above TZS 11m) since 2013; VFD software alternative since 2020; Protocol 2.1 mandatory since 6 January 2021; pre-clearance CTC migration proposed in the 2025/26 Budget (no firm statutory date yet)
model: Fiscal-device model (EFD/VFD) with mandatory real-time transmission to the Electronic Fiscal Device Management System (EFDMS); migrating toward a token-based pre-clearance (CTC) model, not yet in force
format: Bespoke TRA EFDMS XML schema (SHA1-with-RSA signed) — no Peppol, EN 16931, or UBL alignment
authority: Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA) — Mainland; Zanzibar Revenue Authority (ZRA) operates a separate VFMS regime for Zanzibar
summary: Tanzania has operated mandatory fiscalisation since 2010, when Electronic Fiscal Devices (EFDs) became mandatory for VAT-registered traders (Phase 1); this extended to non-VAT traders above TZS 11 million turnover in 2013 (Phase 2). A software-based Virtual Fiscal Device (VFD) alternative became available in 2020, and all devices were required to run Protocol 2.1 (enabling input-VAT verification codes) from 6 January 2021. Every fiscal receipt is signed on-device and transmitted in real time to the central EFDMS using a bespoke TRA XML schema — not Peppol, EN 16931, or UBL. The 2025/26 Budget proposed deeper EFDMS integration and a pre-clearance step, but this has no firm statutory effective date yet. Mainland Tanzania and Zanzibar operate separate regimes: Zanzibar has its own Virtual Fiscal Management System (VFMS) under the Zanzibar Revenue Authority (ZRA), with different VAT rates. Finance Act 2024 updated EFD penalties (now up to TZS 4,000,000 and/or 3 years' imprisonment for failure to issue/use an EFD), and Finance Act 2025 introduced VAT withholding and a reduced 16% VAT rate for electronically-paid B2C supplies from September 2025.

name: Thailand
keyDate: B2B issue since voluntary system launched 2017
format: XML (ETDA Standard 3-2560); PDF/A-3 on the email track
summary: Thailand operates a voluntary e-Tax Invoice and e-Receipt system under the Revenue Department, with ETDA setting technical standards. As of July 2026 there is no legislated B2B, B2G, or B2C mandate. Opt-in issuers send documents to buyers and report XML data to the Revenue Department by the 15th of the following month; paper remains valid and adoption is driven by tax incentives.

name: Timor-Leste
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Timor-Leste in the sources reviewed. ATTL's own site describes only e-Tax (general online return filing) and a bilateral VAT-implementation cooperation visit from the Australian Taxation Office (3-7 August 2026) — no e-invoicing-specific system or mandate.

name: Togo
keyDate: B2B since 2026 Finance Law (Law No. 2025-002, approved by the National Assembly 29 December 2025, effective 1 January 2026) introduces a certified e-invoicing obligation for B2B VAT taxpayers; implementation timeline and platform details to be set by ministerial regulation
model: Not yet finalised — OTR will set up or approve e-invoicing platform(s) and collect transaction data electronically; standardised paper invoices remain in use until the new system is implemented
format: Certified electronic invoice — created, transmitted, received, and archived electronically; specific technical format not yet published
summary: Togo's 2026 Finance Law (Law No. 2025-002), approved by the National Assembly on 29 December 2025 and effective 1 January 2026, introduces a certified electronic invoicing obligation for B2B VAT transactions and, notably, in cases where a taxable person requests advance payment. Certified e-invoices must be created, transmitted, received, and stored electronically, regardless of the technology used, provided they comply with legal requirements. The Office Togolais des Recettes (OTR) will set up or approve e-invoicing platform(s) and collect transaction data electronically, with implementation details and a specific rollout timeline to be defined by the finance minister's implementing regulations — not yet published as of this dossier. Until the new system is implemented, standardised paper invoices remain in use. This builds on a longer-standing context in which electronic invoicing has been legally equivalent to paper invoicing in Togo since 2018, though used only voluntarily to date.

name: Tokelau
keyDate: No mandate
summary: Tokelau is a non-self-governing territory within the Realm of New Zealand with a very small economy supported primarily by fisheries licence fees and New Zealand budget support. No e-invoicing mandate, platform, or programme of any kind has been identified for Tokelau. New Zealand's own e-invoicing programme, built on the Peppol framework, does not extend to Tokelau.

name: Tonga
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
authority: Ministry of Revenue and Customs, Tonga
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Tonga in the sources reviewed. The other banked sources (Thomson Reuters general e-invoicing overview, Basware's New Zealand compliance page) are not Tonga-specific and were excluded. No Tonga-specific evidence was found.

name: Trinidad & Tobago
keyDate: No mandate published
summary: Trinidad and Tobago has no published national electronic invoicing mandate. The Inland Revenue Division (IRD) runs eTax for online tax returns and account management; that service is not a structured invoice clearance regime. On the official pages reviewed, VAT still runs on ordinary invoices and periodic returns under the VAT Act.

name: Tunisia
keyDate: B2B issue since 1 January 2026
authority: DGI (Direction Générale des Impôts) / TTN (Tunisie TradeNet)
summary: Tunisia's El Fatoora platform, operated via Tunisie TradeNet (TTN) under DGI oversight, is mandatory for B2G transactions by large enterprises overseen by the Large Enterprises Directorate and for B2B transactions in the medicines and fuel supply chains (retail excluded). A draft 2026 Finance Law published on 14 October 2025 proposed extending mandatory e-invoicing to all service transactions from 1 January 2026; later 2026 reporting treats that law as enacted (Article 53) and the services extension as in force from that date. A penalty framework under the 2025 Finance Law (Article 71) has applied since 1 July 2025; authorities have signalled a soft landing for SMEs after the 2026 expansion, and B2C is not yet mandatory.

name: Türkiye
keyDate: B2B since Mandatory since 2014; current general threshold 1 January 2026
authority: Turkish Revenue Administration (GİB — Gelir İdaresi Başkanlığı)
summary: Türkiye operates one of the world's most mature continuous transaction control regimes, with e-Fatura (clearance) covering B2B and B2G transactions and e-Arşiv (quasi real time reporting) covering B2C and smaller B2B transactions. Both systems are administered by GİB and use the UBL-TR XML format with mandatory digital signatures. Thresholds have been progressively lowered since 2014, with the general e-Fatura threshold standing at TRY 3 million annual gross sales from 1 January 2026 and sector specific thresholds as low as TRY 500,000 for e-commerce, real estate, motor vehicles, construction, and intermediary sectors.

name: Turkmenistan
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Turkmenistan in the sources reviewed. Confirmed still dead on this pass — consistent with the country's earlier exclusion from the 85-country discovery batch this session.

name: Turks & Caicos Islands
keyDate: No mandate
authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Turks and Caicos Islands
summary: The Turks and Caicos Islands has no e-invoicing mandate, platform, or announced programme. The territory operates a narrow tax base centred on customs duties, accommodation tax, stamp duty, and sector-specific levies, with no income tax, corporation tax, or VAT. The Inland Revenue Department's recent modernisation activity is limited to automated remittance form distribution and field compliance visits, neither of which involves e-invoicing.

A "mirror Code" US territory — the US Internal Revenue Code is mirrored as its own internal tax law, administered locally by the VI Bureau of Internal Revenue. No e-invoicing mandate found. (Added 10 August 2026 as part of an ISO 3166-1 territory-coverage audit — confirmed case-by-case, not assumed from constitutional status alone.)

name: Uganda
keyDate: B2B since EFRIS mandatory for VAT-registered taxpayers since 1 January 2021; expanded to 12 additional business sectors (including certain non-VAT-registered entities) from 1 July 2025 per General Notice No. 2218 of 2025
model: Clearance — invoice generated and encrypted, transmitted to EFRIS for real-time decryption, validation and certification (QR code, verification code, invoice ID, fiscal document number) before delivery to the customer
format: Structured digital format via EFRIS (system-to-system, client application, URA web portal, or USSD)
summary: Uganda operates the Electronic Fiscal Receipting and Invoicing Solution (EFRIS), administered by the Uganda Revenue Authority (URA) under the Tax Procedures Code Act (Cap. 343) and the Tax Procedures Code (Electronic Invoicing and Receipting) Regulations, S.I. No. 82 of 2020. Mandatory for all VAT-registered taxpayers since 1 January 2021, the mandate was significantly expanded from 1 July 2025 — per General Notice No. 2218 of 2025 — to cover twelve additional business sectors, including certain non-VAT-registered entities operating in designated industries. Invoices generated via ERP system-to-system connection, client application, the URA web portal, or USSD are encrypted, transmitted to EFRIS, validated in real time, and returned with a QR code, verification code, invoice identification number and fiscal document number before being issued to the customer.

name: Ukraine
keyDate: B2B since B2G mandatory since 2011; URTI/ERPN registration for B2B/B2C above UAH 1m turnover since 2015; full VAT invoice digitisation since 2018; SAF-T mandatory for large taxpayers from 1 January 2025, all VAT-registered taxpayers from 1 January 2027
model: Clearance-style registration — VAT invoices must be registered in the Unified Register of Tax Invoices (URTI/ERPN) before/at issuance to grant input VAT credit
format: National XML, registered via URTI/ERPN; SAF-T reports in standard XML format
summary: Ukraine has progressively built one of the longer-standing continuous-transaction-control regimes in the region. B2G e-invoicing became mandatory in 2011. The Unified Register of Tax Invoices (URTI, also referred to as ERPN) was introduced in 2015, effectively mandating e-invoicing for B2B/B2C transactions once a supplier's turnover exceeds UAH 1 million. Full VAT invoice digitisation followed in 2018: all VAT-registered taxpayers must issue tax invoices electronically and register them with the tax authority before or at the time of issuing them to customers. A COVID/war-driven moratorium on fines ran from March 2020 through 26 May 2022, with a grace period to 15 July 2022 to register February-May 2022 backlogged invoices without penalty. Standard Audit File for Tax (SAF-T) reporting began as an optional pilot in 2023, becomes mandatory for large taxpayers from 1 January 2025 (annual filing plus on-demand submission within 2 business days of an audit request), and extends to all VAT-registered taxpayers from 1 January 2027. Ukraine does not currently provide pre-filled VAT returns despite receiving invoice data in real time — the State Tax Service uses e-invoice data to cross-check taxpayer-submitted declarations after the fact.

name: United Arab Emirates
keyDate: B2B from 1 January 2027
authority: Ministry of Finance / Federal Tax Authority
summary: Pilot phase opened July 2026. B2B and B2G e-invoicing via accredited service providers becomes mandatory for large businesses (revenue of AED 50 million or more) on 1 January 2027 and for all other VAT-registered businesses on 1 July 2027. In-scope government entities go live on 1 October 2027.

name: United Kingdom
keyDate: B2B issue from 1 April 2029
summary: The UK's 2025 public consultation on e-invoicing (HMRC and the Department for Business and Trade, closed May 2025) resulted in a confirmed decision at the Autumn Budget 2025 (November 2025): e-invoicing for all VAT invoices, covering B2B and B2G, will be mandatory from 1 April 2029. Real-time reporting to HMRC is not included, at least initially. HMRC's 2026 Tax Update 2026: Simplification, Modernisation and Fairness policy paper confirmed Peppol as the core interoperability network. A detailed implementation roadmap is due at Budget 2026. NHS suppliers already use Peppol-based e-invoicing today (in force since 2019); MTD for VAT digital reporting has applied to businesses over £10,000 turnover since April 2023.

name: United States
keyDate: end of FY 2018
summary: No federal e-invoicing mandate exists (no VAT). The Digital Business Networks Alliance operates a voluntary market exchange framework, and e-invoicing developments in the US are tracked at the state level. Federal agencies were directed to electronic invoicing for appropriate procurements by the end of FY 2018 under OMB Memorandum M-15-19, with supplier channels set by contract rather than a single national format.

name: Uruguay
keyDate: B2B issue since 1 January 2025
summary: Uruguay was an early Latin American mover on e-invoicing: DGI's e-CFE (Comprobante Fiscal Electrónico) system began with the largest taxpayers on 1 August 2012 and phased in over more than a decade, reaching roughly 98% of invoices nationwide by late 2024. Rather than a grace period after the start date, Uruguay managed the rollout through gradual phased deadlines and extensions, with the final push to the end of 2024 acting as a de facto grace period; full enforcement for all VAT payers, including small businesses (IVA mínimo) and independent professionals, began 1 January 2025. Every e-CFE must be digitally signed and authorised by DGI in real time via a unique CAE code before it carries legal effect.

name: Uzbekistan
keyDate: B2B issue since 1 January 2026
summary: Uzbekistan requires electronic invoices under a live clearance model run by the State Tax Committee. Invoices are issued as structured JSON, digitally signed, and validated before they become legally final, covering B2G, B2B and B2C. Since 1 January 2026 the system also scores invoice risk in real time and prepares tax returns from cleared invoice data.

name: Vanuatu
keyDate: B2B since No confirmed mandate; VSMS planned Aug 2025 to Jan 2026
summary: Vanuatu has no confirmed legal e-invoicing or transaction level CTC mandate in official sources. A Value Added Tax Monitoring System (VSMS) on Data Tech International's TaxCore was reported in August 2025 as planned for rollout from August 2025 to January 2026, led by Inland Revenue; that window has elapsed without independent confirmation of completion. We continue to monitor for official confirmation.

name: Vatican City
keyDate: No mandate
authority: Amministrazione del Patrimonio della Sede Apostolica (APSA)
summary: Vatican City operates its own independent tax administration, distinct from any parent/host state, but no e-invoicing mandate, platform, or credible programme has been found. Sovereign city-state with its own administration and negligible commercial economy relative to a typical country. No e-invoicing mandate or need for one was found. (Added 10 August 2026 as part of an ISO 3166-1 territory-coverage audit — confirmed case-by-case, not assumed from constitutional status alone.)

name: Venezuela
keyDate: B2B issue since March 2025 (anticipated implementation date per SENIAT)
summary: Venezuela operates a mandatory fiscalised invoicing regime administered by SENIAT, under which businesses must use either authorised fiscal machines or SENIAT-approved digital invoicing systems. In late 2024 SENIAT issued Administrative Ruling No. SNAT/2024/000102, which regulates the use of digital media for the issuance of invoices and other tax documentation, with implementation anticipated for March 2025. The ruling covers entities transacting via electronic means or web portals and introduces digital invoicing as an alternative to fiscal machines for qualifying taxpayers.

name: Vietnam
keyDate: B2B issue since 1 July 2022
format: National structured XML, GDT technical standards
summary: Vietnam has mandated structured e-invoicing for essentially all taxpayers since 1 July 2022 under Decree 123/2020/ND-CP, administered by the General Department of Taxation (GDT). E-invoices are either authenticated (granted a tax-authority authorisation code before delivery to the buyer, a clearance-style flow) or unauthenticated (sent directly by the seller without prior authorisation, for eligible taxpayers). Decree 70/2025/ND-CP and Circular 32/2025, effective 1 June 2025, updated the framework to address practical gaps and align with the amended VAT Law; from 1 July 2026 Decree 254/2026/ND-CP and Circular 91/2026/TT-BTC replace those instruments under the 2025 Law on Tax Administration.

name: Wallis & Futuna
keyDate: No mandate
authority: Service des Douanes et Contributions Diverses, Wallis-et-Futuna
summary: Wallis and Futuna is a French overseas collectivity with its own autonomous customs and indirect-tax administration, the Service des Douanes et Contributions Diverses, operating independently from metropolitan France. No e-invoicing mandate, platform, or credible programme has been identified for the territory. France's national e-invoicing reform, phasing from September 2026, does not extend to Wallis and Futuna, which lies outside the scope of French VAT law.

name: Western Sahara
keyDate: No mandate
authority: No independent tax administration; Moroccan DGI administers areas under Moroccan control
summary: Western Sahara is a disputed territory with no independent tax administration. The majority of the territory is administered in practice by Morocco's Direction Générale des Impôts (DGI), which is developing its own national e-invoicing reform, but no e-invoicing mandate applies to Western Sahara as a distinct jurisdiction. No independent e-invoicing framework, platform, or legal instrument exists for Western Sahara.

name: Yemen
keyDate: No evidence of an e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found in the sources reviewed
summary: No evidence of a concrete e-invoicing mandate, platform, or specific legislative proposal was found for Yemen in the sources reviewed. The vendor page explicitly states: 'The Yemen Tax Authority (YTA) ... could lead e-invoicing compliance if implemented, though no formal system exists yet.' YTA's own official site shows only tender notices and general tax administration content, no e-invoicing mention.

name: Zambia
keyDate: B2B issue since Mandatory from 1 July 2024; penalties from 1 October 2024
format: Smart Invoice via VSDC API or ZRA apps
summary: Zambia’s ZRA Smart Invoice system is live. VAT registered taxpayers must issue invoices through approved Smart Invoice applications or a certified integration so that ZRA can validate each invoice and apply a Mark ID and QR code. The mandate started on 1 July 2024 after a 19 March 2024 launch; penalties for not using the system have applied since 1 October 2024.

name: Zimbabwe
keyDate: B2B issue since Buyer-detail transmission mandatory from 31 May 2025
model: Fiscalisation clearance (real-time transmission to ZIMRA FDMS at point of sale)
format: No prescribed inter-party format; FDMS clearance via hardware device or API; QR code required on output invoice
summary: Zimbabwe operates a mandatory fiscalisation regime under which all VAT-registered operators and, more broadly, all taxpayers must transmit invoice data to ZIMRA's Fiscalisation Data Management System in real time via approved hardware devices or a virtual API. Invoices are cleared through the FDMS portal and must carry a verifiable QR code; only fiscalised invoices that comply with Section 20(4) of the VAT Act are accepted for input tax claims. A May 2025 directive extended the obligation to include mandatory transmission of buyer details such as name, address, TIN and VAT registration number.
